docs/handoff/01-current-state-and-evidence.md

Current state and evidence

1. Checkpoint and provenance

The baseline for this handoff is Coven Castles · Orchestration Atlas, private Site version 3 (renamed Coven Compass on 2026-11-19; see D01), published from commit d7b6f1e655140036cca49f31687131352162de13 on 18 November 2026.

The export adds documentation, portable test fixtures, packaging/checking utilities, a Handoff link/reader, mission-navigation/mobile changes, and the scalable layout, viewport, density, sample-control, and crown refinement. The combined source also incorporates replay/adaptive-mobile work from 07919b421df5457e778e1b1c6a73512c8f27ba73. It is not a byte-for-byte export of the older v3 commit or either pre-combination branch. HANDOFF_MANIFEST.json identifies the baseline and inventories the exported files; CHECKSUMS.sha256 records their bytes. A publication receipt, when recorded, identifies its particular artifact and must not be inferred from an earlier checkpoint.

This source grew from the supplied Coven Castles v27 prototype. “v27” is the inherited prototype name; Site version 3 is the publication checkpoint. They are distinct version systems.

2. Status vocabulary

LabelMeaning here
Implemented — prototypePresent in the packaged simulation source
Verified — unitExecuted in Node fixtures with a limited DOM facade
Observed — publication imageVisible in the generated preview for the exact saved Site version
Specified constraintSupplied by the owner as an architectural requirement
ProposedRecommended design or implementation sequence requiring canonical mapping and acceptance
Unknown / unverifiedNo current repository, packaged-runtime, remote-host, or security evidence was established

Do not convert any one label into another. A prototype UI event is not a daemon receipt; a unit fixture is not a real-host test; a publication image is not keyboard or mobile acceptance.

3. Implemented behavior

The application is buildless HTML, CSS, SVG, and JavaScript. The scene/UI source is joined by the pure layout and viewport helpers and the canonical crown renderer listed below. It has no bundled application framework or npm dependency graph. The inherited optional Google Fonts request has system-font fallbacks.

The simulation starts with four Projects, seven missions, and 114 delegated agents. It supports Project/mission selection, familiar highlighting, detailed tasks and agent rows, synthetic event replay, locally simulated decisions and Psyche conversations, adjustable familiar presentation, and an isolated Seal lab. Activity may change with the simulation clock. Browser display preferences do not constitute durable mission or identity state.

The simplified map uses one representation for all overview projects. It shows familiar groups inside a project, and individual agent dots only for the selected mission. Pending decision counts sit on project boundaries. The Projects drawer overlays the map, and familiar chips sit beneath it. These relationships are presentation behavior, not permission boundaries implemented by a backend.

The current refinement is implemented; combined source-level verification passed. It uses uniform four-corner overview Projects, aspect-aware paired placement, shared coordination corridors ending at inward gates, and full/compact/tiny density modes. At full detail, each overview Project has at most eight mission seals plus overflow; compact/tiny views use exact aggregates. The complete mission collection remains available through search and drilldown. Explicit Coven/project scope is separate from zoom; measured chrome-safe fitting refits on resize only in auto-fit mode. The scene crown extrudes the exact canonical silhouette without replacing flat UI marks. Guide 15

The Project browser adds project search and 8/16/32/64/128 sample presets. Reset removes only generated layoutDemo additions, preserving baseline and user-created Projects; existing project counts may exceed a requested preset. The previous cosmetic 16-Project and 12-mission creation caps are removed. Presets and bounded geometry tests do not establish production capacity or unlimited browser performance.

The combined mobile workspace reuses the original replay and camera controls in Map, Missions, Activity, and View surfaces. Shared live replay preserves elapsed time and playing/paused state across project focus changes, while imported recordings keep their own extent. Delayed reports do not force a replay to the live edge. Visible chrome is measured after the current HUD/manifest structure is updated; keyboard visibility, camera lock, and manual framing constrain refit. Selection cleanup during replay restores the saved camera and its auto-fit policy. These are local presentation/replay semantics, not a daemon clock or durable execution state. 5. Verified baseline evidence

Current evidence: generated, not hand-written

Current counts live in one file, tests/evidence/current.json (../../tests/evidence/current.json). node scripts/verify-all.mjs runs the static source checker, the Node suite, the crown check, a handoff build, ZIP verification, and the source/test/crown/manifest checks in a clean extraction of the built ZIP, then writes the counts it measured. CI runs node scripts/verify-all.mjs --check on every pull request and fails if that file is stale. --report PATH adds the commit, runtimes, time, and per-step results for one run; CI uploads that report as a workflow artifact. Evidence level: static + unit only.

Browser QA — 2026-11-19 (headless Chromium)

scripts/browser-qa.mjs ran at commit b3970fd in headless Chromium 130.0.6723.31 (Playwright 1.48.2, installed outside the repository) against python3 -m http.server. It made 201 browser checks, 201 passed, 0 failed (record (../../tests/evidence/browser-qa-2026-11-19.json)):

  • Simulation mode, both default and ?source=simulation, at 1440×900, 390×844 and 844×390. The map renders and the settled fit keeps every Project in the stage. A Project opens from the Projects drawer, and a mission opens from the mission browser (the mobile dock's Missions on phones) with its inspector visible. Replay starts and moves the cursor. Seal lab opens and closes. The mobile dock shows on phones and is hidden on desktop. No console errors, page errors or failed requests (Google Fonts excluded).

  • Every ?source=fixture scenario, and ?source=live, at the same sizes. The simulation never boots: #app is hidden and the Atlas header is not mounted. The state label and message match each scenario. The Projects table is present with the right row count, or absent. There's no horizontal page scroll and no clipped table.

The run found one bug, in the fixture table layout at phone width, which was fixed in b3970fd before the recorded run. Screenshots stay outside the repository. This is browser-engine evidence. It does not establish Safari, physical devices, real multi-touch, keyboard-only use, screen readers, or daemon behavior.

Later runs of the same script added checks that mission names clear the local Psyche crown and each other, and that familiar labels clear each other and the mission names, after opening a Project and on the replay frame. They found a second bug. In project scope, mission names covered the crown and ran into each other at every viewport, and familiar labels piled up in landscape. It was fixed in 877c7ce and cf04a8b. At cf04a8b the script made 225 browser checks, 225 passed (record (../../tests/evidence/browser-qa-2026-11-19-mission-names.json)). On the layout before 877c7ce, the mission-name checks fail 12 times.

Everything after this subsection is a dated historical record. It keeps its counts as recorded and is not updated with later changes. Other documents link here or to current.json instead of repeating counts, and scripts/check-source.mjs enforces that.

At the v3 checkpoint, seven Node tests passed with zero failures or skips. They cover mission insertion/removal across replay without a wall-count change; hidden agents before selection; selected-mission agents, reserved places, gate links and gate decisions; familiar filters within projects; local/global selection consistency; unchanged seal logic; and all six seal states across three detail tiers after normalizing the ground origin.

sealOf, buildSeal, and drawSeal matched the earlier v2 source at 494a08f6bf10c9a0606c82e86821fed8a253f066. The meaningful presentation change set the shared ground plane to zero. The bundled tests/fixtures/v2-index.html is extracted from that exact source path and commit; baseline.json records its digest. The test loader verifies the fixture before comparison, without requiring .git.

JavaScript syntax, linked static assets, unique static IDs, CSS delimiters, and patch whitespace were also checked. The generated publication image for saved v3 was visually inspected and showed the simplified Coven overview. That observation did not exercise controls or demonstrate responsive behavior.

At the v3 checkpoint, native browser access was blocked by browser URL policy. No workaround was used. Browser focus, touch, keyboard, responsive layout, and dynamic browser interactions were unverified in that historical record.

docs/handoff/02-architecture-and-ownership.md

Architecture and ownership

Decision and evidence boundary

Use the Compass Site as a presentation and interaction reference for existing OpenCoven systems. Keep authoritative state transitions in Coven, orchestration meaning in Psyche, and identity governance in the Familiar Contract. Coven Host should make this work discoverable in a folder and across devices; it should not introduce another daemon, identity root, scheduler, or competing state database. These are the user's architectural requirements, not claims that every production repository already implements them. U1

The historical Site baseline is commit d7b6f1e655140036cca49f31687131352162de13. The bundle also contains subsequent mobile/navigation work and the scalable layout/crown refinement, which is implemented and source-level verified. Its README continues to identify the application as a local simulation. Production repositories, their current APIs, and packaged runtime behavior were not inspected for this handoff. Treat the integration below as proposed until repository discovery establishes the existing contracts and tests. Export provenance identifies the delivered source separately from historical checkpoints. S1

Use these labels consistently during implementation:

LabelMeaning in this handoff
Source-inspectedA property visible in the bundled Site source.
Supplied requirementA boundary or invariant established by the user's instructions.
ProposedA recommended integration design requiring implementation and review.
Discovery requiredThe corresponding production component, contract, or behavior has not been established.
VerifiedReserved for an identified artifact and a recorded acceptance check; never inferred from a mockup.

What the bundled Site actually supplies

The Site reduces sample events into browser-side worlds using apply, advances or reconstructs them with seek, and appends simulation events with emit. canAct distinguishes live sample interaction from recorded/replay modes. These functions demonstrate interaction behavior; they are not principal authentication, protected authorization, durable scheduling, or a production event log. The store helper uses browser local storage for presentation-related persistence. S2

Proposed data and authority flow

This diagram shows responsibilities, not a proposed set of deployed services. Threads and Psyche may be implemented within existing packages or processes; discover those locations first. The SDK and read projection are constrained client surfaces. U1

flowchart TD
    P["Human principal"] --> C["Cave · CLI · Psyche Build · Host"]
    C --> S["Canonical SDK"]
    S --> D["Coven daemon"]
    T["Threads authorization rules"] -.-> D
    Y["Psyche orchestration semantics"] -.-> D
    D --> R["Qualified execution runtime"]
    D --> V["Read projection"]
    V --> C

An authenticated principal requests an operation through a client. Coven resolves the exact familiar root/revision, checks the operation against authoritative authorization and lifecycle state, and commits through the existing canonical transition mechanism. The final authorization check and commit must share the same immutable snapshot or be atomic. A resulting projection makes the outcome visible; it does not retroactively authorize it. U1

For integration, maintain a mapping worksheet rather than immediately defining a new wire schema. Establish where the existing contracts provide: project identity; exact familiar binding; mission/task/attempt identifiers; lifecycle state; input and policy revisions; runtime capability evidence; pending decisions; operation outcomes; receipts; and subscription freshness. Missing information remains unavailable until its owner supplies it. Client-generated identifiers may correlate a request but may not establish identity, permissions, or ownership.

Identity, orchestration, and execution remain distinct

A familiar's glyph and hue help people recognize continuity. They are not the familiar's root, revision, principal binding, or authorization. A delegated worker is an execution participant with a task/attempt relationship; it is not automatically a newly governed familiar. The same familiar can appear in multiple projects without creating multiple identity roots. Bind every executable session to the exact authorized familiar revision through the owning contract. U1

Likewise, a “mission” in the Site should map to an existing canonical orchestration object only after its lifecycle and scope match. Do not rename a job, routine, run, or session into a mission merely because both have a title and status. The adapter may compose a display from existing objects while preserving their original identifiers and relationships.

A runtime being able to launch a process does not establish that it can durably cancel, recover, isolate, or account for that process. Qualification evidence must accompany the capability used by the integration. A UI should degrade to an inspectable proposal when the required capability or authoritative evidence is unavailable. U1

Preserve visual meaning without overstating evidence

The source seal has six states: Planned, Active, Needs you, Stalled, Sealed, and Broken. It gives each council familiar a wedge, derives progress from role-owned targets, and uses the rim for the tightest time/token/budget limit. The renderer applies a 12-degree minimum wedge, an eight-wedge ceiling, and a twelve-working-pip cap per familiar. Those display limits must remain visible in exact detail; they must not become limits on the canonical underlying model. S1 S2

The production adapter needs additional freshness and availability information alongside lifecycle state. Disconnected, stale, reconciling, rejected, and unavailable cannot honestly be painted Active simply because the last snapshot was active. Keep the six visual states where their meanings fit, and supply a separate factual freshness indicator. Unknown progress must not become zero; absent evidence must not become success.

“Sealed” should mean the defined acceptance criteria have authoritative evidence. The current simulation derives it from modeled target and artifact counters, so it cannot prove a production acceptance result. “Broken” currently follows a limit-paused mission once no open request takes precedence; the Inbox offers “Keep stopped.” Preserve that behavior in the demo, but map production refusal, pause, cancellation, and failure states deliberately instead of collapsing them. S2

Discovery deliverable and decision gate

Before implementation, assign an owner to a compact evidence ledger with one row per integration concern:

  1. Record the repository, exact revision, scoped instructions, and public entry point.

  2. Identify the authoritative object, storage owner, and transition function.

  3. Trace authentication, authorization, revocation, commit, and receipt paths.

  4. Record supported snapshot/subscription behavior and its gap/recovery contract.

  5. Link tests and packaged/live evidence separately; mark missing checks explicitly.

  6. Decide whether the change belongs in an existing SDK adapter, daemon handler, Psyche semantic module, or presentation component.

The gate is a reviewed mapping showing one owner for each authoritative transition. If discovery finds overlapping stores or ambiguous ownership, resolve that first. U1

Continue with the integration proposal and Host folder, sync, and recovery.

Sources

  • U1 — supplied architectural and engineering instructions.

  • S1 — Site scope and evidence limitations.

  • S2 — simulation, projection, and seal implementation.

  • S3 — presentation adapter; S4 — semantic scene styling.

  • S5 — isolated seal explorer; S6 — source-level fixtures (../../tests/presentation.test.cjs).

docs/handoff/03-integration-proposal.md

Integration proposal: from simulation to one canonical mission

Recommended first delivery

Connect one existing project and one familiar to an observational Compass view, then qualify one bounded task through the existing Coven/Psyche path. Expand to durable remote execution and Host synchronization only after the same operation can be inspected, refused, cancelled, and recovered through canonical interfaces.

Everything in this document is proposed integration work. The bundled Site currently mounts CovenAtlas with local snapshot, navigation, familiar-highlight, and legend functions. Its chat, approval, and activity behavior modifies sample worlds; it is not a production transport or SDK. Do not replace a function with a network call and assume the resulting application has inherited the necessary authority model. S1 S2 S3

Delivery sequence and ownership

StageConcrete workPrimary owner to establishExit evidence
0. DiscoverMap exact production objects, public clients, lifecycle rules, and packaged entry points.Existing repository owners across Coven, Psyche, SDK, and Compass.Revision-pinned contract map; unresolved assumptions assigned.
1. Isolate presentationSeparate sample data generation from rendering and selection. Preserve the standalone demo.Existing production UI/client owner, informed by Cave and Brand.Demo remains explicit; operational mode cannot invoke sample mutation.
2. ObserveRead one project's canonical snapshot and follow updates without writes.SDK adapter plus Coven read surface.Correct initial state, duplicate handling, gap detection, reconnect, and unavailable states.
3. ProposeSubmit a bounded proposal and render its actual decision/receipt lifecycle.Threads/Coven integration through canonical SDK.Unauthorized, stale, replayed, and revoked requests refuse correctly.
4. ExecuteRun one task with fixed inputs, a qualified runtime, fenced attempt ownership, and durable evidence.Coven execution applying Psyche semantics.One attributable attempt; acceptance evidence tied to exact inputs.
5. RecoverExercise cancellation, process loss, lost acknowledgments, and restart.Coven/Psyche with runtime qualification.No stale-owner commit or silent duplicate effect; unresolved outcomes remain visible.
6. Extend HostSynchronize eligible artifacts and proposals under one authoritative owner.Existing Host/workspace integration owner discovered in stage 0.Conflict, offline, path-safety, and recovery cases in the companion document.

These are acceptance stages, not a promise that the production repositories currently contain the required interfaces. Keep each stage in the existing owning component where possible. U1

Separate the two execution modes

The current event reducer, sample trace, automatic activity generator, replay tools, and Seal lab are valuable as a deterministic presentation fixture or explicitly labeled sandbox. Keep their writes within a demo-only adapter. In connected mode, a sample event must have no route to authoritative state. Conversely, replaying historical production evidence must not enable live command buttons merely because the browser changes its live flag. S2

Create a small adapter boundary with four responsibilities: obtain canonical read data; maintain subscription freshness; submit an allowed proposal/command through the SDK; and retrieve its authoritative result. Those are responsibilities, not proposed public method names or a new canonical schema. Translate the existing production contract into the presentation model, retaining source identifiers and provenance.

Do not ship mixed-mode fallback that silently substitutes sample missions when the daemon disconnects. Show the last known snapshot with its age, or an explicit unavailable state. The optional demo remains a separately selected experience.

Read-model and subscription requirements

First discover whether the canonical interface offers snapshots, event cursors, revisions, or another consistency mechanism. The adapter must know the scope and consistency point of its initial snapshot before applying subsequent updates. A timestamp alone does not establish an ordered, gap-free stream.

Require a defined strategy for duplicate delivery, ordering, cursor expiration, and object removal. On a detectable gap, stop claiming freshness, enter reconciling state, and acquire a compatible authoritative snapshot. Apply a replacement snapshot and its cursor together; do not merge an old project list with new mission counts. Cache invalidation must respect owner changes and authorization changes as well as data revision.

Every displayed aggregate needs a counting rule. Identify whether an “agent” is an active worker, an allocated participant, an attempt, or historical execution. Count shared-task participants once under the agreed rule. Keep mission assignment, worker lifecycle, and familiar identity distinct. The simulation currently derives these counts from its in-memory maps; that makes its totals internally useful, not a production definition. S2

Read access is itself scoped. The server must filter inaccessible projects and evidence; hiding them in the SVG is insufficient. Preserve exact counters and source records in accessible detail even when the map aggregates or clamps visual marks. U1 S2

Authoritative command path

For the first command, choose an operation already supported by the canonical interface and bounded enough to inspect safely. Discover its actual SDK call and CLI equivalent; this handoff deliberately invents neither.

Discover the supported local/remote transport and its origin, authentication, and session-binding rules. A privately hosted Site is not inherently a trusted daemon client. Do not place reusable credentials in URLs or ordinary browser storage, and do not introduce an ad hoc bridge that bypasses the canonical client boundary.

The server-side path must establish the authenticated principal, exact familiar root/revision, operation-specific authority, target scope, expected object revision, and applicable limits. A caller-supplied role, claimed owner, project path, or model-generated approval is input to validate, not authority. The final authorization decision and commit must be atomic or use the same immutable state snapshot. U1

The client sends the canonical request and then represents the returned outcome faithfully:

  • Proposal retained: the request is inspectable but has not been committed.

  • Accepted for processing: work may be pending; this is not a success receipt.

  • Rejected or expired: display the reason and the authoritative state needed to revise the proposal.

  • Committed/completed: show the corresponding receipt and evidence at their actual scope.

  • Outcome unknown: preserve the request identity and query its result; do not label failure or retry a potentially accepted effect blindly.

Use the existing idempotency/replay mechanism where available. If discovery finds none, the owner must design and qualify it before enabling a retrying write client. Reusing a correlation identifier does not by itself provide idempotency. Retries must also satisfy current routine/mission lifecycle, authorization, input revision, and resource policies.

Long-running lanes, leases, and attempts

Before a task starts, resolve its immutable execution inputs: familiar root/revision, task intent, acceptance criteria, project/worktree revision, content digests, permitted paths/actions, runtime descriptor, and budget/time boundaries. Use the canonical reference/version mechanisms; do not mint a parallel task package format without discovery.

Psyche should define how the work occupies a lane, how a lease is acquired or renewed, what constitutes an attempt, and which conditions permit retry. Coven should persist and enforce those transitions. A worker must carry the current attempt and fencing identity to every protected write or effect-commit boundary. A heartbeat alone is not proof of current ownership. U1

Keep the goal durable across attempts. Proposed follow-up tasks need explicit dependencies, completion criteria, and bounded admission. Classify refusals and failures as terminal, blocked, or eligible for a particular retry policy. A refusal before ownership must not leave a run indefinitely “running” when its lifecycle prevents any valid retry; settle it or record an actionable recovery state.

After lease loss, an old worker may still run or return output. Its result may be retained as uncommitted evidence, but it must not overwrite a newer attempt or publish a protected result. Reacquiring the same task requires the canonical ownership transition and a new valid fence where the model requires one. Neither the UI nor a synced lock file may perform that transition.

For Psyche Build, use its existing coding/worktree integrations after discovery. A lane should work from an identified revision in an isolated worktree or equivalent supported workspace; it must not concurrently rewrite a human's active tree. Coven Code supplies execution through the selected runtime path. Build presents the same task, attempt, approval, and receipt objects used by the CLI and Cave rather than tracking a second lifecycle.

Acceptance should bind evidence to inputs. A passing test from one revision cannot qualify another revision by title. Distinguish a produced artifact, a recorded test result, an approved publication, and a provider-confirmed external effect.

Effects, cancellation, and recovery

Before an external effect, persist the canonical intent and the relationship to the current attempt. Use supported provider idempotency or reconciliation where available. Do not promise exactly-once execution across an arbitrary external system: an effect may be accepted before its acknowledgment is recorded.

Cancellation has at least two observable moments: the request was committed, and the relevant execution/effect state was settled. Show that distinction. Stop admission of new work, revoke or invalidate further protected writes according to policy, request runtime cancellation, and reconcile outstanding effects. Cancellation cannot undo a provider-accepted action by changing a local status field.

On restart, recover from durable authoritative state. Reconcile attempts against runtime/provider evidence, expire or reassign ownership through the canonical mechanism, and retain uncertainty when the external outcome is unknowable. Resource accounting should likewise distinguish observed usage, reservations, and unresolved consumption; delayed reports cannot justify an invented hard-spend guarantee.

Qualification matrix

For each case, capture the exact code/artifact revision, principal and fixture scope, request/attempt identifiers, observed transitions, and receipts. Start with the smallest relevant test, then use real-daemon or packaged-artifact tests wherever mocks could hide the failure. U1

CaseRequired result
Snapshot followed by duplicated updatesStable state and counts; no repeated operation.
Subscription gap or expired cursorExplicit reconciling state followed by a consistent snapshot.
Identity revision or authorization changes before commitRevalidation rejects or degrades the request; no stale grant.
Same request retried after an acknowledgment is lostExisting outcome is found or uncertainty remains explicit.
Worker loses its lease and returns lateSuperseded attempt cannot commit protected output.
Cancel races with provider acceptanceReceipt distinguishes cancellation intent from external outcome.
Daemon/process failure during transitionRecovery produces a justified state without contradictory receipts.
Offline or stale client submits a decisionProposal remains pending or is refused; client never self-commits.
Second host tries to acquire the same workSingle-owner rules and fencing prevent competing commits.

The bundled source-level fixtures remain a useful visual regression floor, with the README recording their limited coverage. They do not satisfy this matrix. Browser interaction and responsive checks for the current revision also remain separately required. S1 S6 (../../tests/presentation.test.cjs)

Implementation packets and rollout decision

Give each implementation agent a bounded packet: owning repository and exact starting revision; scoped instructions; the existing contract to extend; the invariant being repaired; allowed changes; acceptance commands discovered from that repository; and required evidence. Require a red-to-green example for authority or lifecycle bugs and preserve unrelated work. U1

Start with an adapter-focused change and one end-to-end qualification case. Expand only when the evidence supports the next stage. Keep disconnected observation usable, preserve demo isolation, and retain a clear path back to the previous client presentation. Merging, releasing, production deployment, paid infrastructure, and external communications require their own applicable authorization; producing this handoff has not performed any of them. U1

Sources

  • U1 — canonical ownership, atomic authorization, and engineering requirements.

  • S1 — current Site scope and verification limitations.

  • S2 — local reducer, replay, command simulation, and snapshot implementation.

  • S3 — current presentation adapter; S6 — source-level regression fixtures (../../tests/presentation.test.cjs).

docs/handoff/04-host-folder-sync-and-recovery.md

Coven Host: folder, sync, and recovery proposal

Product model and first boundary

Make Coven Host a familiar place to find project work, proposals, artifacts, and receipts while Coven remains the authority that executes and commits. A folder can make work portable and reviewable without becoming the source of identity or permission. The user's instructions require one coherent authority model and treat cloud infrastructure as an execution surface, not the fundamental home of a familiar. U1

This document is a proposal. The Site's Project metadata includes illustrative repository and root strings, but it does not mount folders, synchronize files, or connect to a remote daemon. The production Project schema, Host implementation, filesystem layout, and transport must be discovered before choosing exact filenames or APIs. S1 S2

The first sync delivery should use one authoritative owner per project/run. It may distribute eligible content and display remote results, but it should not support opportunistic offline ownership takeover or replicate live daemon databases.

Proposed folder contents

The paths below illustrate a user experience, not a required new directory standard. Reuse existing Project/package conventions when discovery finds them. Ordinary file permissions can reduce accidental edits, but authoritative validation remains necessary.

Illustrative locationIntended contentTreatment
<Host>/Projects/<project>/workspace/User work and approved execution inputs.Versioned working material; never implicit permission to execute.
…/proposals/Draft intents, requested changes, and imported suggestions.Pending until accepted through the canonical authority path.
…/artifacts/Produced reports, patches, exports, and supporting evidence.Bind each accepted version to content identity and its attempt.
…/receipts/Exported copies of authoritative outcomes.Read-only projection; edited copies do not rewrite history.
…/references/Links or exported context identifying the project and familiar revision.References, not private identity material or executable grants.
…/.cache/Replaceable previews and downloaded content.Discardable; excluded from authoritative recovery decisions.

Keep daemon databases, WAL/SHM files, runtime sockets, process handles, live lease state, bearer tokens, private keys, provider credentials, and secret-bearing environment files outside the synchronized set. A backup/export facility may handle selected state separately under its own consistency and access rules; generic folder sync must not copy a live database and call the result a recoverable authority.

Discover the existing credential facility and secret-redaction rules. The folder should reference an approved credential binding without containing the credential itself. Protect exports and logs too: an apparently harmless report can contain paths, prompts, access tokens, or confidential source content.

File edits create input, not committed control state

A user can edit a brief or project file in their normal editor. A watcher should detect the changed version, preserve the prior base, and prepare an inspectable proposal or new input version. It must not interpret a line such as “approved,” “owner,” or “run now” as an authenticated operation. Model output, downloaded content, and files synchronized from another machine are subject to the same rule. U1

For a running attempt, keep the input snapshot immutable. Later file edits become a candidate next version; they do not silently alter the work already authorized. A user may explicitly request a new attempt or revision through the canonical client, subject to its cancellation and acceptance rules.

Exported receipts should retain their source identifiers and integrity/provenance information. A content digest identifies bytes; it does not alone authenticate who produced them or prove that an operation was authorized. Importing a JSONL trace from the demo is also a replay operation, not an admission path into production authority. S2

Proposed synchronization cycle

  1. Inventory bounded content. Compare eligible paths against a known base version. Record byte identity, type, size, and applicable project/input references using existing mechanisms where available.

  2. Stage transfers. Transfer incomplete content into a private staging area with quotas and cancellation support. Do not expose partial content as the accepted project version.

  3. Verify the destination. Check received bytes, path policy, content limits, and provenance before publication. A matching checksum is necessary for integrity, but does not confer authority.

  4. Publish a consistent version. Use the platform's supported atomic publication mechanism for the defined unit. Do not infer an atomic multi-file update from several successful file copies.

  5. Reconcile canonical state. Submit eligible proposals or acknowledge artifact availability through the existing SDK/daemon path. Keep transfer completion separate from task acceptance or protected commit.

  6. Advance the sync checkpoint. Retain enough base and transfer information to resume or explain interruption. The checkpoint is sync bookkeeping, not a competing task database.

The exact transfer provider is a discovery decision. Prefer existing transport and storage capabilities over introducing another service. Define bandwidth, storage, retention, and cost boundaries before enabling remote transfer; this handoff does not create a paid account or select an unverified provider.

Conflict policy

Avoid timestamp-based last-writer-wins for semantically important files. Filesystem modification times are useful observations, not an authority ordering rule. Compare against a common base and preserve both versions when their relationship is uncertain.

ConflictProposed handling
Same input edited on two hostsPreserve both candidates and their common base; require review before choosing execution input.
User edits a file while an attempt produces outputKeep attempt output separate; present a patch or merge proposal against the recorded input revision.
Brief, permissions, identity reference, or ownership changesRoute a proposal to the relevant canonical owner; never auto-merge into authority.
Receipt bytes differ for the same claimed outcomeQuarantine the conflicting copy and retrieve/reconcile the authoritative record.
Delete races with edit or remote resultRetain a tombstone and recovery copy under a defined retention policy; do not silently delete new work.
Rename or case/Unicode collisionResolve identity and filesystem constraints explicitly; do not treat conflicting paths as the same approved object.
Cache differsRebuild from an accepted source; cache conflict never decides mission state.

Textual auto-merge may be offered as a draft for ordinary source files. Its success does not establish semantic correctness, authorization, or acceptance. Keep protected metadata and external-effect decisions outside automatic merge.

Offline operation

Offline users can inspect the last known state, edit ordinary work, and prepare proposals. Label the projection with its known revision/freshness. New control changes remain proposal-only until the authoritative owner can validate and commit them. Local connectivity loss must not manufacture an approval receipt or a new owner epoch.

An already-running local attempt may continue only if the existing execution/authorization model explicitly permits that behavior with valid inputs and bounded authority. If required revocation, ownership, or lease evidence cannot be established, stop further protected commits and expose the degraded state. Do not assume that a cached permission remains valid indefinitely.

On reconnect, first re-establish authoritative identity, ownership, and object revisions. Then compare queued proposals with their bases. Stale proposals may need rebasing or renewed approval; replaying the offline queue in file timestamp order is insufficient. These rules follow the supplied separation of intent, authority, and committed state. U1

Multiple hosts and remote execution

Distinguish the authoritative owner, the execution host, and a viewing/syncing client. A remote runtime can execute a bounded attempt while the owner retains the canonical task and decision state. A copied workspace does not transfer ownership.

Any future ownership transfer must use the canonical serialized transition, advance its ownership/fencing state, and ensure that the former owner cannot commit afterward. A local PID, shared-folder lock, heartbeat, or file named “owner” does not provide that guarantee. If there is no reachable shared authority capable of resolving competing owners, a partitioned client cannot safely prove exclusive takeover. For the first delivery, retain a fixed owner and make failover an explicit, qualified operation. U1

Remote attempts need exact input references, scoped access, runtime capability evidence, and fencing at every relevant commit boundary. Preventing local state commits alone is insufficient when a stale worker can still invoke an external provider; use supported credential/effect admission boundaries and reconcile any uncertain provider outcome.

Cancellation should record intent durably, stop admitting additional effects, request runtime termination, and settle outstanding results. A transfer may finish after cancellation; retain it as attributable evidence without promoting it into an accepted result automatically. Cancellation does not retract an already accepted external action.

Path safety and filesystem acceptance

Implement path validation in the owning file-operation layer, not solely in the UI. Enforce the approved root at the actual open/write operation. Reject traversal, unexpected absolute paths, ambiguous separators, unsafe device/special files, and out-of-scope links. Account for case handling and platform-specific reserved names before mapping remote names to local paths.

Symlink checks must survive replacement between validation and use. Prefer descriptor-relative, no-follow, or equivalent platform mechanisms; re-resolving a string and later opening it is not a complete race defense. Establish policy for hard links and mount changes as well. Download/archive extraction must apply the same rules, plus file-count, expanded-size, and depth limits.

Publish through staging that stays on an appropriate filesystem and preserves the promised atomicity. Test interrupted writes, disk-full conditions, permission failures, and integrity mismatches. Report a failed transfer or failed persistence barrier explicitly rather than showing a new accepted revision.

Recovery and acceptance packet

On restart, load authoritative state first, reconcile ownership and attempts, then rebuild folder projections. Treat orphaned staged transfers as incomplete. Verify durable artifact references, reconcile missing receipts or unknown external outcomes, and admit new work only after the necessary authority and state are available.

ExerciseAcceptance evidence
Crash after content upload but before publicationPartial content remains unaccepted; restart resumes or discards safely.
Crash after effect acceptance but before receipt visibilityReconciliation finds the outcome or preserves explicit uncertainty.
Symlink/root replacement during a writeOut-of-scope target is never modified.
Two hosts edit/delete the same inputBoth candidates and the conflict decision remain inspectable.
Old owner returns after transferIts fenced attempt cannot commit protected changes.
Offline proposal uses a revoked/stale bindingReconnection refuses or requests renewed authorization.
Sync scans a live database or secretExclusion policy prevents transfer; diagnostics avoid leaking contents.

Assign discovery of folder conventions to the Project/Host owner, authoritative transitions to Coven/Psyche, protected decisions to Threads integration, public bindings to SDK, and cross-client acceptance to Cave, CLI, and Psyche Build owners. Each packet should identify real modules and tests after discovery. U1

The acceptance result is a recoverable relationship between files, exact inputs, authority, attempts, and receipts. A folder that merely looks synchronized is not enough.

Sources

  • U1 — supplied authority, identity, persistence, and client boundaries.

  • S1 — simulation scope and absence of production integration.

  • S2 — illustrative Project metadata, local replay, and sample decisions.

  • Related: architecture and ownership, integration stages and qualification.

docs/handoff/05-implementation-plan.md

Implementation plan: from visual simulation to canonical orchestration

Status and scope

Proposed production work. The design input began with the v3 Site at revision d7b6f1e655140036cca49f31687131352162de13; the bundle also contains subsequent mobile/navigation work and the scalable Atlas layout/crown refinement. The latter is implemented and source-level verified. The buildless JavaScript/SVG interface, local event reducer, sample decisions, replay, and seal laboratory remain a presentation reference. They do not establish a daemon integration, production authorization, remote execution, or durable orchestration service. Record actual delivered source and packaging separately from historical baseline evidence.

Paths such as README.md, dist/index.html, and tests/presentation.test.cjs are relative to the bundle root. Read the shared source ledger and docs/handoff/source-context/user-architecture-instructions.md before implementation. API names, repository locations, and supported protocol versions remain TBD through canonical repository discovery. “Coven Host,” “Compass” (formerly “Castles”), and “CLI” describe requested integration surfaces; their existing ownership and implementation must be verified.

The intended result is one coherent path from a human-readable project and mission view to authoritative state, bounded work, and auditable outcomes. Keep the familiar identity distinct from its delegated agents. Preserve the visual grammar while replacing sample data with a constrained projection of canonical records.

Ownership to confirm

ComponentResponsibility to preserve
Familiar ContractGoverned identity, exact authorized root and revision.
SPARContinuity profile/query plane; no second identity root or database.
Coven ThreadsProtected-surface authorization and proposal-versus-commit decisions.
PsycheCanonical task, lane, lease, approval, receipt, retry, and recovery semantics.
CovenDaemon authority, persistence, sessions, runtime execution, authoritative transitions.
Coven HostDiscover its actual role; bind remote execution/access to canonical Coven authority.
Coven Runtimes / SDKRuntime capability conformance and constrained canonical client bindings.
Compass / CaveProject-scope visualization and human oversight; discover where production UI belongs.
Psyche Build / CLICoding cockpit and terminal clients consuming the same authorized objects. Discover the CLI’s relationship to Coven Code.

These boundaries are design constraints, not evidence that every component already exposes the required capability. Before adding any service, schema, storage, or adapter, establish whether an existing component owns it.

Phase 0 — repository and contract discovery

W01 · Pin the integration surface

Owner: integration lead with each repository maintainer. Dependencies: none. Discover: scoped AGENTS.md, README, ADRs, package/lock files, schemas, CI, release artifacts, worktree state, and relevant open work. Inventory actual repositories and revisions without modifying unrelated changes. Map requested names to current components; record unavailable repositories explicitly.

Acceptance: a versioned owner map identifies authority, client, persistence, identity, runtime, and deployment boundaries. Evidence: exact revisions, file references, commands, and unresolved access questions. A missing contract produces a discovery issue, not a guessed API.

W02 · Establish the canonical object and transition map

Owner: Psyche, Coven, Threads, Familiar Contract, and SDK maintainers. Dependencies: W01. Discover: project/scope, mission/task, familiar/session, agent/attempt, proposal/decision, lease/fence, event/cursor, receipt, cancellation, and limit definitions. Identify authentication, atomic authorization/commit behavior, idempotency rules, and supported compatibility policy.

Acceptance: every displayed quantity and proposed command maps to a canonical field or an explicit missing capability. Differentiate an agent identity, execution attempt, and lease. Evidence: source-backed mapping and a proposed contract change only where an existing owner needs one. This is the first integration gate.

Phase 1 — read-only canonical projection

W03 · Implement the constrained read adapter

Owner: SDK and the existing client/projection owner. Dependencies: W02. Discover: authenticated snapshot/query APIs, event subscriptions, pagination, cursor semantics, ordering, and reconnect behavior. Implement the smallest supported adapter; preserve revisions and provenance in its output. Do not move the prototype’s apply() or emit() reducer into a new authoritative service.

Acceptance: a canonical fixture or daemon snapshot produces the expected view; event gaps suspend claims of freshness and trigger supported reconciliation. Evidence: adapter tests, recorded input versions, and a real-daemon read trace when available. No protected write is required for this phase.

W04 · Bind the visual grammar to source-backed facts

Owner: Compass/Cave UI owner with Psyche review. Dependencies: W03; static component work may proceed after W02. Discover: existing UI components, accessibility conventions, and navigation ownership. Replace atlasSnapshot() sample totals with adapter-derived data. Keep uniform project boundaries, mission seals, familiar identity marks, selected-mission agent dots, and boundary decision entry points.

Acceptance: exact counts remain available beside minimum-angle and pip-cap encodings; stale/disconnected/reconciling are explicit connection conditions, separate from the six mission states. Missing data never becomes zero by default. Evidence: projection fixtures, interaction/accessibility results, and traceable seal calculations.

Phase 2 — authenticated proposals and decisions

W05 · Enforce the protected command boundary

Owner: Coven Threads and Coven, consuming Psyche contracts. Dependencies: W02; W03 provides readback. Discover: principal authentication, session binding, authorization objects, immutable snapshots, revocation checks, replay defense, and durable receipts. Build the supported proposal/decision route in its canonical owner. Treat every client field as untrusted.

Acceptance: final authorization and commit are atomic or use the same immutable authorized snapshot. Wrong principal, identity revision, scope, stale authorization, or replay cannot produce a protected effect. Evidence: red-to-green boundary tests at the enforcing server, including revocation between proposal and decision. UI-only checks cannot close this packet.

W06 · Present pending, rejected, and uncertain outcomes accurately

Owner: Compass/Cave and SDK. Dependencies: W05. Discover: decision request/result shapes and operation-status lookup. Replace the local resolve() simulation with proposal submission and authoritative readback. Submission remains pending until a canonical outcome is known; transport loss produces an explicit unknown outcome.

Acceptance: the boundary square opens relevant pending decisions, review displays actual operation and scope, and duplicate input cannot duplicate execution. Rejection or a lost acknowledgement never causes an automatic permission retry. Evidence: UI contract tests and server receipts correlated to a single operation identity.

Phase 3 — bounded execution in one Project

W07 · Connect one scoped execution path

Owner: Coven, Psyche, and Coven Runtimes. Dependencies: W05 and runtime capability discovery. Discover: supported runtime descriptors, task assignment, lane scheduling, lease acquisition, fencing, workspace boundaries, and result receipts. Choose a reversible pilot task within a specifically authorized project scope. Bind execution to the exact familiar root/revision and authorized operation.

Acceptance: one canonical mission can create bounded work, expose its attempts, and produce durable receipts. A stale worker or substituted identity cannot commit. Evidence: real runtime/daemon integration, lease/fence observations, allowed/denied side-effect checks, and cleanup records.

W08 · Make cancellation and limits authoritative

Owner: Psyche and Coven; clients expose results. Dependencies: W07. Discover: cancellation races, attempt completion, elapsed/token/budget accounting, reservation rules, and retry ownership. Define the observable behavior for an in-flight effect when cancellation arrives; do not promise rollback unless a canonical operation supports it.

Acceptance: reaching a bound stops further unauthorized work, increasing a limit follows protected authorization, and cancellation distinguishes requested, accepted, stopping, and terminal outcomes where the canon supports them. Evidence: deterministic race tests and daemon restart tests. A coral rim is a warning projection, never enforcement.

Phase 4 — Host synchronization and recovery

W09 · Bind remote Host execution to existing authority

Owner: verified Coven Host owner with Coven, Runtimes, and identity maintainers. Dependencies: W07 and W01’s deployment inventory. Discover: trust establishment, credential placement, host enrollment, session scopes, network assumptions, capability negotiation, and where durable state lives.

Acceptance: remote placement changes the execution surface without creating another identity root or authorization authority. An untrusted or incompatible host cannot acquire protected capability by claiming it. Evidence: an explicit trust/data-flow diagram, capability failure tests, and authenticated remote execution under a bounded pilot principal.

W10 · Recover without duplicate effects or invented truth

Owner: Coven/Psyche persistence and Host transport owners. Dependencies: W09. Discover: acknowledgements, durable cursors, reconnect snapshots, conflict policy, operation lookup, fencing persistence, and recovery ownership. Exercise lost messages and host/daemon restarts at transition boundaries.

Acceptance: unknown outcomes reconcile against canonical receipts; repeated events converge without repeating effects; stale leases cannot regain authority; synchronization conflicts remain explicit until canonically resolved. Evidence: reproducible fault-injection traces with operation IDs, event positions, authority revisions, final state, and side-effect counts.

Phase 5 — Psyche Build, CLI, and Cave parity

W11 · Integrate Psyche Build as a canonical consumer

Owner: Psyche Build and SDK. Dependencies: W03–W08; remote features wait for W10. Discover: existing task/lane views, proposal surfaces, receipt links, coding workspaces, and recovery UI. Preserve Build’s specialized cockpit without inventing an independent scheduler or approval store.

Acceptance: Build and Compass show the same underlying mission, attempt, proposal, and receipt identities. A changed view does not change authority. Evidence: a shared scenario replayed through both clients and canonical state comparisons.

W12 · Verify packaged CLI and oversight parity

Owner: actual CLI/Coven Code owner, Cave, SDK, and packaging maintainers. Dependencies: W05–W08. Discover: real supported commands, machine-readable output, exit behavior, configuration, authentication, and packaged entry points. Document discovered commands only after verifying them.

Acceptance: packaged CLI, Cave, Build, and Compass preserve pending/committed/rejected/unknown distinctions and point to the same receipts. Noninteractive use fails closed when required authority is absent. Evidence: installed-package tests and a cross-client operation matrix; source imports alone do not prove the shipped CLI works.

Phase 6 — packaging and bounded pilot gates

W13 · Produce a reproducible review package

Owner: release/package owner and integration lead. Dependencies: relevant client work and contract compatibility decisions. Discover: current release policy, artifact signing/checksums, supported platforms, upgrade behavior, and CI gates. Keep the Site handoff ZIP distinct from a production release.

Acceptance: the exported source verifies without Git history, contains accurate provenance, excludes secrets/runtime data, and exposes known limitations. Production packages meet their existing gates. Evidence: checksums, clean extraction validation, packaged-client results, and exact command logs.

W14 · Run an explicitly bounded pilot

Owner: principal/product owner with Coven, Host, and client maintainers. Dependencies: W10–W13 and all applicable acceptance gates. Discover: authorized principals, project scope, runtime capabilities, limits, observability, recovery ownership, and rollback procedure.

Acceptance: the agreed workload completes with inspectable authorization and receipts; injected failures recover as specified; no unexplained or duplicate protected effects remain. Evidence: the matrix in 07-validation-and-acceptance.md, unresolved-risk register, and explicit publication/deployment authorization. Do not infer production readiness from the visual prototype or unit suite.

Sequencing rule

Advance by evidence rather than calendar dates. Discovery unlocks parallel projection, enforcement, and runtime work against the same pinned contracts. Protected effects wait for enforcement; remote execution waits for bounded local execution; cross-client acceptance waits for authoritative results. Packaging can prepare early, but a pilot cannot bypass unfinished authority, recovery, or compatibility gates.

docs/handoff/06-execution-playbook.md

Execution playbook

Establish a reproducible starting point

The historical design/prototype reference is v3 revision d7b6f1e655140036cca49f31687131352162de13. The handoff adds documentation, portable validation, packaging, later mobile/navigation work, and the scalable layout/crown refinement. The latter is implemented and source-level verified. Consult the source ledger and final export provenance; do not describe the entire export as byte-identical to v3.

From the extracted bundle root, inspect README.md, the source ledger, docs/handoff/source-context/user-architecture-instructions.md, and the package manifest before running anything. The Site needs no npm installation or bundler. Record the actual runtime versions and run these source/package checks:

node --version
python3 --version
node scripts/check-source.mjs
node --test tests/*.test.cjs
node scripts/test-atlas-crown.mjs
python3 scripts/verify-handoff.py .

Record the actual current test count and outcomes. The suite uses extracted functions and shared modules with DOM facades and numeric inputs; it has no browser layout engine or native-device emulation. The separate crown check preserves the canonical path and aperture. The export includes the presentation comparison baseline with provenance so these tests can run outside Git. Confirm that behavior in a clean extraction; an earlier Git-backed run alone is insufficient evidence for portable packaging.

For archive inspection or rebuilding, discover the supported arguments before use:

python3 scripts/build-handoff.py --help
python3 scripts/verify-handoff.py --help

The standard output is dist/downloads/Coven_Compass_Handoff_2026-11-19.zip. Verify a generated ZIP by passing its path to the verifier. Keep generated archives, .git, environment files, credentials, and runtime data outside archive contents. A successful source check is neither a security audit nor a production build result.

For a recipient’s local preview, where local browser access is permitted:

python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory dist

Open the local server in that environment and stop it when finished. Do not expose it publicly or bypass a browser/network policy to obtain a preview. Native browser navigation for the v3 revision was policy-blocked; the separate recorded static overview preview proves only what appears in that image.

The historical pre-layout Chrome interaction/mobile pass and its Node test result are recorded in MOBILE_READINESS.md. Those fingerprints do not verify the current scalable layout, crown, viewport, density, or sample controls. Headless Chromium QA of the current source ran on 2026-11-19 (record (../../tests/evidence/browser-qa-2026-11-19.json), summarized in chapter 01); it does not establish Safari, physical-device, real multi-touch, keyboard-only, or screen-reader acceptance. Keep these evidence periods separate and record permitted future browser acceptance against the exact source tested. Historical JSON audits remain in the export; repository-only browser screenshots do not.

Discover real repositories before proposing commands

In each available candidate checkout, start read-only:

git status --short --branch
git rev-parse HEAD
rg --files -g AGENTS.md -g 'README*' -g '*schema*' -g '*receipt*' -g '*lease*' -g '*identity*' -g '*auth*' -g '*sync*' -g '*test*' -g '*lock*' -g '*.yml' -g '*.yaml'
rg -n 'proposal|authorization|receipt|lease|fenc|revocation|reconcile|idempot|cursor' .

Use scoped searches after locating the owner directories. Inspect instructions, ADRs, schemas, tests, CI, and release evidence. Preserve unrelated changes; use a permitted isolated branch/worktree when appropriate. Record unsupported or unavailable capabilities explicitly. These are discovery commands, not evidence that any particular Coven subcommand, endpoint, schema, or release pipeline exists.

For each contract, record its owning repository, pinned revision, authoritative definition, consumers, test entry point, and compatibility constraints. Find the canonical command through repository documentation and the real program’s supported help interface before adding CLI examples. Never translate the prototype’s local event names into supposed public APIs without this evidence.

Work lanes and integration order

LaneWork packetsSafe parallel workIntegration prerequisite
A: contracts and ownershipW01–W02Repository inventory, source ledger, identity/data-flow mappingReviewed owner and contract map
B: projection and UIW03–W04, W06Read adapters, sealed fixtures, visual componentsCanonical read contracts; decisions wait for W05
C: authorityW05Server enforcement, negative tests, receipt semanticsAuthenticated principal and exact identity contracts
D: executionW07–W08Runtime capability discovery and bounded fixturesW05 before any protected effect
E: Host recoveryW09–W10Trust model and fault harness discoveryBounded local execution and canonical persistence
F: client parityW11–W12Existing client inventory, presentation adaptersStable command/outcome contracts
G: packaging and pilotW13–W14Export manifests, validation scripts, acceptance planningRequired authority, recovery, and packaged-client evidence

The integration lead owns sequencing, not a new control plane. Assign file ownership before simultaneous edits. Contracts and shared fixtures should land before dependent clients; do not let several lanes redefine the same operation schema. Keep contract changes reviewable separately from presentation changes when practical.

Integrate one canonical read path first. Then add one proposal-to-receipt path, one bounded execution path, and its cancellation/recovery cases. Extend that proven path to Host, Build, CLI, and Cave. A branch can be ready for review while deployment remains blocked by missing authorization or evidence.

Packet execution loop

  1. Read the packet’s dependencies and current source, then pin the exact revisions actually used. Compare them with the handoff reference; explain any intentional drift.

  2. State the invariant, authoritative owner, allowed scope, and evidence required. For an authority defect, reproduce the failing boundary before patching it.

  3. Make the smallest coherent change in the existing owner. Keep the Site simulation separate from production fixtures and services.

  4. Run the narrowest meaningful test first. Expand only for a concrete integration risk or required gate; use real-daemon, remote, or packaged-client tests when a source-only test cannot prove the invariant.

  5. Inspect the diff and artifacts for unrelated changes, leaked runtime data, misleading state labels, and missing provenance. Record exact results.

  6. Commit/review according to existing authorization and repository policy. Update the packet ledger, hand off dependencies, and continue to the next unblocked packet.

Do not turn transient network failure into permission to resubmit a protected operation. Use a canonical status query or reconciliation path keyed to the original operation; otherwise report uncertainty and preserve the pending/unknown state. Rejected, revoked, or expired authority requires the canonically defined resolution, not repeated attempts.

Evidence and resumable checkpoints

Every packet should leave this record, including incomplete work:

Packet / owner:
Prototype reference: d7b6f1e655140036cca49f31687131352162de13
Implementation repositories and exact revisions:
Status: implemented | verified | proposed | blocked | unknown
Invariant and canonical owner:
Changed files / public contract changes:
Commands, environment, exit codes, and results:
Evidence level: static | unit | browser | daemon | packaged CLI | remote Host
Operation / receipt / event-cursor references, when applicable:
Skipped checks and why:
Unresolved risks / next dependent packet:
Authorization needed for any external action:

Persist the record beside the repository’s normal issue/PR evidence. Include a precise next step and working-tree status so another agent can resume without repeating discovery or interpreting a proposal as an approval. Redact credentials; retain nonsensitive correlation identifiers necessary to inspect outcomes.

Stop only for material access, ownership, policy, or authority ambiguity that prevents safe progress. Continue independent read-only work and reversible authorized implementation. Explain the exact blocking rule and evidence required to resolve it; do not ask broad approval questions when the current session already authorizes the work.

docs/handoff/07-validation-and-acceptance.md

Validation and acceptance

Current scalable-layout refinement

Implemented; combined source-level verification passed. node scripts/verify-all.mjs runs the suite, crown, and static source checks, then clean-extraction, rebuilding, and archive verification, repeating the suite and crown/source checks in the extracted copy. Current counts are in tests/evidence/current.json (../../tests/evidence/current.json). The earlier layout branch's package pass and the incoming replay branch's Node/Chrome pass remain historical checkpoints in current state and evidence. Commands:

node scripts/check-source.mjs
node --test --test-reporter=tap tests/*.test.cjs
node scripts/test-atlas-crown.mjs

The layout module's sweep covers selected project counts through 128 (0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 64, and 128) as geometric correctness cases; mission packing covers every integer count from 0 through 128. It is not a load test or production benchmark. Headless Chromium QA of the current source ran on 2026-11-19 (record (../../tests/evidence/browser-qa-2026-11-19.json), summarized in chapter 01); it does not establish Safari, physical-device, real multi-touch, keyboard-only, or screen-reader acceptance. Historical pre-layout Chrome records and source fingerprints do not establish visual or interaction acceptance of the new layout, density modes, sample controls, crown, or fit behavior. Guide 15 supplies the current presentation contract and remaining browser cases.

Historical v3 baseline evidence

The source reference is v3 d7b6f1e655140036cca49f31687131352162de13. The local simulation and its renderer are implemented. node --test tests/presentation.test.cjs was rerun against that source: seven tests passed; zero failed, cancelled, or skipped. The original comparison baseline is 494a08f6bf10c9a0606c82e86821fed8a253f066; handoff tooling makes that baseline portable and records its provenance.

The seven fixtures exercise these actual extracted functions and behaviors:

  1. Overview mission seals add, remove, and return during replay without a change in the four-wall project count.

  2. Agents, reserved places, and gate links remain hidden without a selected mission.

  3. Selection reveals only the chosen mission’s agents, reserved places, links, and gate decisions.

  4. A familiar filter highlights relevant missions and groups within project scope.

  5. Local familiar selection clears a conflicting global filter; a familiar chip replaces local selection consistently.

  6. v27 seal functions/constants and their numerical meanings match the pinned baseline, apart from the normalized ground origin.

  7. Geometry matches that baseline across six states and three detail tiers after ground normalization.

These are Node unit tests using a DOM facade, not browser execution, accessibility, CSS/layout, or runtime integration tests. The portable suite reads and verifies the bundled v2 baseline fixture rather than inspecting an arbitrary Git checkout.

The source ledger records a generated static preview for the saved v3 Site version, associated with the same v3 revision. Its inspected overview image supports a visual observation of the simplified composition only. Native browser navigation was blocked by URL policy at that checkpoint; interaction, focus, responsive, and reduced-motion behavior were not verified by that historical record.

Historical pre-layout mobile verification

Before the scalable-layout refinement, the mobile pass ran node --test tests/*.test.cjs with no failures. MOBILE_READINESS.md records that historical test count, navigation, gesture, overlay, and mission-interaction coverage, its settled Chrome layout audits, observed browser flows, and remaining checks. These results supplement the original seven-test baseline; they are not the current source-suite total or a current browser pass. Chrome viewport stress tests also do not establish native iOS keyboard or device acceptance.

The source/package checkers and clean-extraction verification supply additional export evidence when run and recorded. They do not establish a real daemon, installed CLI, remote Host, security review, production conformance, or pilot acceptance. Those remain unknown/unverified until the following gates are satisfied.

Visual and projection acceptance

Preserve angular project scope, circular missions, stable familiar identity marks, selected-mission agent dots, boundary decisions, and Psyche coordination. Confirm that each tier exposes the intended detail, including keyboard navigation and a meaningful focus return after drawers/dialogs close. Test actual browser interactions at supported viewport sizes and reduced-motion settings.

For the new overview, test uniform four-corner Projects, compact paired placement, non-intersecting reserved rectangles, and shared corridor routes ending at inward gates. Inspect full/compact/tiny density transitions, up to eight miniature seals plus an exact remainder, aggregate counts, and the full searchable mission collection. Exercise project search, 8/16/32/64/128 sample presets, and reset without removing baseline or user-created Projects. Verify that the removed cosmetic creation caps do not reappear as navigation limits.

Keep Coven/project scope explicit across pan, zoom, orbit, search, and history navigation. Fit must include the measured chrome-safe viewport and visible crown/label bounds. Resize should refit in auto-fit mode and preserve manual framing otherwise. Inspect the canonical crown aperture at low pitch in both scopes, with flat UI marks unchanged and no spinning or glow. These source contracts still require browser evidence for rendered clearance, focus, touch targets, and readability.

Combined mobile, replay, and fit boundaries

ScenarioRequired behavior
HUD/manifest changes at the compact breakpointUpdate the current lead-card structure before measuring and queuing fit; include a nested mobile HUD at its actual position.
Chrome hidden through CSS or DOM visibilityExclude non-rendered/hidden elements from safe-area reservations; their old rectangles must not shrink the usable map.
Full mobile modal inspectorKeep modal focus/inert ownership; exclude the full modal from canvas-fit reservations while it obscures the inactive map. Reserve ordinary visible nonmodal chrome normally.
Keyboard opens during a queued resizeRecheck keyboard state inside the queued fit; defer automatic reframing while typing, and preserve camera lock/manual mode after it closes.
Replay removes the selected missionClear the stale selection and restore saved zoom/pan together with its saved auto-fit policy; cleanup must not silently re-enable auto-fit.
Adaptive popup closesReuse existing camera-dock/familiar observer notifications to update available space; do not add a second camera or replay state owner.
Project focus during playbackRetain the shared live cursor, elapsed time, and playing/paused state; imported recordings and delayed reports retain their defined boundaries.

Source regressions for these boundaries do not replace a browser pass at the compact breakpoint, with actual keyboard geometry, nested controls, and modal focus behavior. Record the final combined result separately from both branches' earlier evidence.

For every canonical fixture, independently calculate familiar agent shares, owned-target progress, and the tightest time/token/budget limit. Check all six states: Planned, Active, Needs you, Stalled, Sealed, Broken. Near-white indicates a need for human attention; coral indicates at least 85% of the relevant limit or the defined broken-state treatment. Neither color grants authority.

Verify minimum 12° wedges, maximum eight wedges, and maximum twelve working pips per familiar against exact textual counts. A shape enlarged for legibility must not imply a different count. Missing or stale source data must remain explicitly missing/stale. Connection health is separate from mission state; avoid silently turning a disconnected mission into Planned, Stalled, or zero agents.

Authority and recovery test matrix

The canonical owner must define API names and transition details before implementation. The expected authority behavior below is the acceptance invariant, not an invented endpoint contract.

ScenarioInjection and observationExpected authority behaviorRequired evidence
Stale projectionDeliver an old snapshot, then attempt a protected decision using stale context.UI marks stale context; server revalidates current authorized state or rejects the stale decision. Old displayed authority cannot authorize a write.Daemon test, revisions, decision outcome, receipt or rejection.
Disconnected client/HostCut transport during observation and during an operation.Client exposes disconnection/unknown outcome. Execution follows canonical leases and bounds; connectivity loss creates no new authority.Network fault trace, lease state, side-effect count, reconnect result.
Pending proposalSubmit a valid proposal without an authorized decision.Proposal remains pending and visually distinct from committed state; no protected effect occurs.Server persistence and effect checks; UI pending representation.
Invalid identity/sessionSubstitute a root, revision, principal, or unauthorized session binding.Fail closed; no fallback to a name, glyph, model, or nearby revision.Red-to-green server rejection tests and zero protected effects.
Revocation raceRevoke authority after review but before commit.Final verification and commit use the same valid immutable authorization snapshot or reject; stale review cannot bypass revocation.Deterministic race test at enforcing boundary.
Cancellation raceCancel before dispatch, during execution, and concurrently with completion.Report authoritative outcome; prevent future effects as specified. Do not claim completed effects were undone without supported compensation.Daemon/runtime race traces and final receipts.
Lost acknowledgementCommit once, drop response, then reconnect.Reconcile the original operation identity; do not blindly repeat the effect. Unknown remains explicit until resolved.One committed effect, durable receipt, status/recovery trace.
Replay/duplicate decisionRepeat request/event across clients and restarts.Canonical replay/idempotency rules prevent duplicate protected effects. Rejection does not trigger a permission retry.Restart-inclusive tests, original operation identity, effect count.
Lease fencingLet an old worker resume after its lease was replaced.Stale fence cannot write or commit; only canonically authorized ownership proceeds.Runtime/daemon tests covering both old and new workers.
Sync conflictConcurrent clients/hosts propose incompatible updates from different revisions.Apply canonical conflict policy with explicit outcomes; no last-writer-wins elevation of authority or silent proposal promotion.Conflicting revisions, rejected/accepted outcomes, final state.
Event gap/reorderingDrop, duplicate, or reorder events around snapshot recovery.Mark freshness uncertain, use supported reconciliation, converge without duplicate effects; never infer omitted approvals.Cursor/snapshot trace and final-state comparison.
Limit reached/increasedExhaust a bound, then submit an unauthorized increase.Canonical enforcement stops further prohibited work; only a valid protected decision can increase a limit.Measured usage, rejected increase, authorized-path receipt.
Host/daemon restartRestart before persistence, after commit, and before delivery of receipt.Recover only durable authoritative state; retain fencing/replay guarantees and explain uncertain outcomes.Restart fault harness, durable records, effect counts.
Cross-client conflictAct on the same proposal through Cave, CLI, Build, and Compass.Clients share authoritative outcomes; later stale decisions cannot create extra effects or a different permission result.Packaged/client integration matrix and common receipt references.

Evidence gates

Contract gate: W01–W02 identify real owners, versions, enforcement points, and supported compatibility. No production adapter is accepted against fictional APIs.

Read gate: canonical snapshots/events produce correct counts and seals; gaps, unavailable fields, and disconnects are legible. Unit fixtures and real-daemon read traces agree.

Protected-write gate: authority tests run at the enforcing boundary. Each corrected defect has a failing test before the fix and a passing test after it. Include unauthorized principals, scopes, identities, revocation, stale state, replay, and permission-denied behavior. A client-side validator is insufficient.

Execution/recovery gate: one bounded task passes real daemon/runtime tests, cancellation, fencing, limit enforcement, lost acknowledgements, and restart recovery. Extend to a real authenticated Host before claiming remote support. Document any explicitly unsupported fault mode and its safe failure behavior.

Client/package gate: run the actual installed CLI and deployed/test-packaged UI clients against the same supported contracts. Verify authentication/configuration, machine-readable outcomes, error/exit semantics, and receipt correlation. Validate the Site ZIP after clean extraction without Git history; record checker and fixture results separately from production package results.

Pilot gate: agree on principal, project, workload, budget, runtime capabilities, recovery owner, and success criteria before execution. Acceptance requires inspectable authorization, durable outcomes, no unexplained protected effects, and resolution of blocking failures in the matrix. Deployment/publication remains a separate explicitly authorized action.

Record exact commands, exit codes, environments, revisions, operation references, skipped checks, and risks using 06-execution-playbook.md. A passing lower-level gate cannot substitute for a missing higher-level environment. Do not relabel an unrun test as passed because the architecture appears sound.

docs/handoff/08-visual-and-interaction-contract.md

Visual and interaction contract

Implemented in the prototype; proposed as the integration's presentation contract. Preserve the meanings below when replacing fixtures with canonical data. Authoritative operational state belongs to Coven, using Psyche's orchestration semantics, and is exposed through a verified read projection. Shapes, colors, screen positions, and cached labels do not establish authority.

The scalable layout and crown guide supersedes earlier overview positioning and zoom-driven scope assumptions. That refinement is implemented; combined source-level verification passed. It specifies compact paired placement, bounded density, explicit scope, measured fit, and canonical crown relief.
