Headless Chromium QA of the current source ran on 2026-11-19 (record (../../tests/evidence/browser-qa-2026-11-19.json)); historical mobile/Chrome evidence applies only to its recorded pre-layout source.

1. A small vocabulary

ElementMeaningMust not imply
Uniform four-corner Project enclosureOne project's work scopeA runtime sandbox, filesystem permission, authorized execution grant, or four-project limit
Circular divided sealOne mission and its councilA task, familiar identity, or approval token
Familiar glyph and stable hueFamiliar identity within the active bindingThat a display name or color is a globally unique identity
Agent cogOne delegated agent in the selected missionA second familiar identity root
Near-white boundary squareA count of pending decisionsAn approved or completed operation
Psyche crown at the centerCoordination within the displayed scopeThat the model or UI owns daemon authority
Neutral connectionA project participates in this coordination scopeNetwork reachability or active execution by itself
Shared branch corridor and inward gateReadable coordination from Psyche to the destination ProjectExecution dependencies, scheduling order, or authority implied by shared geometry
Mission count inside a ProjectExact known mission totalA limit on the canonical mission collection or evidence of complete data when coverage is partial
Colored connection after familiar selectionThat familiar's assignments in that projectPermission to change all highlighted work
Dotted connectionNo agents assigned in the current complete sample projectionOffline, deleted, or inaccessible data; those require explicit state

Use dist/semantic-map.css for the presentational rules. Keep the canonical crown/lotus already present in dist/index.html; do not substitute the retired symbol or a decorative new mark.

2. Color has a stable job

Familiar hues remain consistent across Projects, mission wedges, group glyphs, and agent marks. Read the current familiar presentation settings rather than scattering colors through new components. A hue is a display aid; the accessible name and exact bound identity belong in the data/details.

Lavender identifies Psyche and its coordination treatment. Near-white marks a decision waiting for the principal. Coral on a seal rim signals a near resource limit or the existing broken-after-limit condition. Do not use a familiar's own hue as a universal success, warning, or error color.

The current sample hues are presentation defaults, not an identity registry or a new brand specification. Where canonical Brand tokens differ, map the same semantic roles through approved tokens and verify contrast. Keep distinct glyphs, labels, fill/outline treatments, and status text so color is never the only signal.

3. Location explains containment

At Coven scale, project enclosures surround Psyche. All projects use the same overview renderer, including the active one. A project should not unexpectedly reveal its entire internal scene simply because it is selected in a different control.

Overview positions come from an aspect-aware compact lattice with opposite pairs, reserved Project/label rectangles, and shared routing corridors. The inward-facing gate terminates the route for that Project. Location is presentation structure, not priority or execution topology. Preserve stable caller ordering; at unchanged geometry options, appending projects retains existing positions. Resizing or explicitly reordering the collection can change placement and must not imply that canonical ownership changed. Current positioning contract

Inside a project, mission seals connect to familiar groups. Selecting a mission reveals its individual agents, reserved positions, task detail, and relevant requests. A round hub identifies an unassigned agent. A square hub identifies an assigned task. Working marks are larger and filled. Idle marks are smaller and hollow. In orbit, cogs have a shallow edge. Working cogs counter-rotate during playback unless reduced motion is enabled. Dashed outlines reserve places for agents at gates. Waiting agents remain inside the boundary. The boundary marker invites review; it does not depict an operation already crossing the boundary.

Within the overview, a boundary marker aggregates pending decisions for that project at its coordination-facing gate. Within a project, markers correspond to the simulation's gate locations and selected-mission scope. A future implementation must map this deliberately from canonical decision data; do not assign a new permission category based on north/east/south/west placement.

Keep internal mission placement and overview project placement distinct. The newer overview helper supersedes the earlier trace/ring positioning assumptions; local mission data still drives each project's contents. Preserve context through filtering, replay, snapshot replacement, and brief changes. A filtered item may dim or disappear; reappearance should not imply it moved between projects. If canonical assignments change, display the actual move as a data change with corresponding details.

4. Topography is measured

Entity placement shares a ground plane. Mission seal relief conveys measured progress; removed terraces, familiar statues, and decorative halo stacks should not reappear as unlabelled “importance.” The requested Psyche crown is a specific decorative extrusion of the exact canonical silhouette, including its aperture. Its height conveys no progress, priority, or authority. Flat UI marks remain flat, and the scene sculpture uses no spin, glow, or gradients. Crown contract

Seal featureCurrent v27 meaning
Wedge angleFamiliar's share of mission agents, subject to the visual minimum
Wedge heightProgress on targets owned by that familiar's roles; unowned targets contribute to every relevant wedge
Wedge brightnessWorking agents are present
Dark lead pipLead familiar's wedge, beginning at twelve o'clock
Central signetMission state: Planned, Active, Needs you, Stalled, Sealed, or Broken
Rim sweepTightest time, token, or budget limit
Coral threshold85% or the existing broken state
Selected-seal edge pipsWorking agents, visually capped per familiar

The renderer permits at most eight council wedges, a minimum wedge angle of 12 degrees, and at most twelve working pips per familiar. Therefore small angular shares and pip counts are not exact numerical displays. Exact counts belong in details. Preserve these qualifications rather than suggesting a miniature seal is a precision chart.

Current progress ownership uses TARGET_ROLES in the prototype. Production integration must inspect canonical target ownership, counters, and completion semantics. Do not copy this fixture mapping into a second orchestration schema. “Sealed” requires canonical completion evidence; a local 100% animation or a model's report is insufficient.

5. Progressive detail and control placement

The Coven view carries boundaries, exact mission counts, decision badges, and a compact identity filter. The Projects drawer is closed by default and overlays the map without changing its dimensions. Project view reveals useful controls and group counts. Mission selection opens task/agent detail. Retain the existing replay and Seal lab as clearly scoped controls.

Project view shows mission seals on a common shallow base. Wedge height adds role-owned progress when the projected seal is large enough to read. The selected mission has a neutral selection ring, a state label, and a single review preview. Its detail pages retain exact agent counts and the Inbox retains every pending decision. Project search and the sample presets keep larger compositions navigable.

Coven and project scope are explicit navigation state, separate from camera zoom. A Fit action uses measured chrome-safe space and enables auto-fit; resize refits only in that mode. Manual camera framing is retained. Camera fitting includes screen-facing crown and label bounds as well as the projected ground. Scope and fit details

Keep the primary path discoverable by keyboard and touch: overview → Project → mission → task/agent/request. Every glyph and boundary marker needs an accessible name and activation behavior. Hidden scene layers must use real visibility removal, not merely zero opacity that leaves invisible tab stops.

Protect navigation and drawer controls from camera drag handlers. A click immediately after a drag must still operate visible chrome. Closing a dialog should restore focus to a visible control; Escape from the Seal lab must not also deselect the underlying mission. Preserve these behaviors during adapter extraction and in the acceptance pass.

6. Real data requires additional explicit states

The simulation's complete in-memory world does not model every production transport failure. Add explicit connection/freshness/coverage treatment before live integration. A disconnected or partial roster must not appear as an empty dormant Project. An unavailable count should be unknown or unavailable, not zero. A retained last-known view must show its revision/time and stale status.

Separate selected, working, waiting, rejected, reconciling, and disconnected states. Selection is local focus. A pending submission or unknown command outcome remains pending/unknown until a canonical receipt resolves it. A rejected request may retain useful context but cannot look committed.

7. Visual acceptance

Use synthetic fixtures and comparable camera states. Inspect the initial Coven overview, every Project, selected missions, familiar filters, empty/dormant projects, pending decisions, the full six-state Seal lab, stale/partial/disconnected data, and the document handoff at desktop and narrow widths. Exercise keyboard focus, screen-reader names, touch targets, contrast, reduced motion, and a zoomed text size.

The existing Node tests verify selected presentation logic and geometry; they do not prove CSS layout or accessibility. The v3 publication image and later pre-layout Chrome records are historical evidence for those specific sources. Headless Chromium QA of the current source ran on 2026-11-19 (record (../../tests/evidence/browser-qa-2026-11-19.json), summarized in chapter 01); it does not establish Safari, physical-device, real multi-touch, keyboard-only, or screen-reader acceptance. Record fresh browser/native evidence for this refinement before treating the rendered contract as accepted, and retain the separate production-integration gates.

docs/handoff/09-security-and-authority.md

Security and authority handoff

Status: proposed integration requirements. The governing ownership rules come from Val’s supplied OpenCoven instructions. Production repository conformance has not been inspected in this handoff. The shipped Compass Site is a local simulation, as documented in README; it neither authenticates a principal to Coven nor executes protected operations.

1. Preserve the trust boundary while replacing the simulation

The current atlasSnapshot() reads local JavaScript worlds, and emit() appends local simulation events. gate.resolved changes those sample worlds. Those functions are useful presentation and replay seams; they are not suitable authorization or durable-commit implementations. The implementation is visible in dist/index.html. No transport adapter should silently reinterpret a local allowed state as a real permit.

Use one authority path. Coven owns authoritative transitions and persistence; Psyche owns orchestration semantics; Coven Threads owns protected-surface authorization and proposal-versus-commit decisions; the SDK exposes constrained canonical bindings. Compass, Cave, CLI, and Psyche Build consume those owners. A Host folder, browser cache, familiar message, or UI control cannot create another writer or authorize itself.

The first live integration should be read-only. Introduce command submission only after the exact existing authentication, operation authorization, replay protection, revocation, and receipt contracts are mapped and tested. Keep the local simulation adapter visibly separate from a daemon adapter. A transport failure must not fall back to simulated success.

2. Identity, intent, authority, orchestration, and execution

ConcernRequired bindingWhat a client may do
IdentityExact authorized familiar root and revision; principal association resolved by the identity/authority ownersDisplay verified references and request an explicit binding; never infer identity from a name, color, or project path
IntentConcrete operation, target scope, immutable input references, requested effect, and bounded parametersDraft and submit an intent through the canonical client
AuthorityAuthenticated principal, operation-specific authorization, freshness/replay rules, revocation/recovery statePresent the decision interface and show returned outcomes; never make the final decision locally
OrchestrationCanonical mission/task/lane/attempt state, leases, retries, recovery and cancellationRender an adapter projection and request supported transitions
ExecutionRuntime capability descriptor, constrained environment, fenced attempt and output provenanceDisplay execution evidence; never treat a process exit or model response as proof of authorized completion

If a familiar changes revision while an attempt is active, use the canonical session-binding policy. Do not hot-swap the revision because the display name is unchanged. Until the policy is verified, hold a proposed rebinding for review and preserve the original attempt’s identity references. SPAR may explain continuity across revisions; it does not grant a new execution identity or become a second identity root.

3. Keep connection, freshness, and work state separate

An active mission can be observed through a disconnected client. A successful receipt can arrive while the map is reconciling an event gap. These must remain distinct axes, rather than collapsing into one green/red status.

AxisProposed presentation vocabularyRequired behavior
ConnectionConnected, disconnected, reconnecting, unavailableDescribe transport availability; never infer that a disconnected remote attempt stopped
Projection qualityFresh, stale, degraded, reconciling, unknownMark incomplete or old views; retain the last observation with its provenance and age
OrchestrationMap the actual canonical states discovered in Psyche/CovenDo not promote the prototype’s six visual seal states into a new normative state machine
Command outcomeDraft, pending, committed, rejected, unknown outcomePending is visually and structurally distinct from committed; unknown means reconcile, not retry blindly

These names are an adapter proposal, not a new canonical enum. Snapshot revisions, ordering/cursor scope, completeness and reset rules must come from existing contracts. A sequence number is meaningful only within its defined owner and stream. On a gap, keep the last verified view, mark it reconciling, and request the supported snapshot/resume path. Do not splice unrelated host streams into an apparently complete ordered history.

A JSON field claiming authenticated, authoritative, or fresh is not proof. The application establishes transport/session trust, validates the canonical envelope and scope, and derives its own observation state. The projection example (../../examples/proposed-atlas-projection.json) deliberately demonstrates a cached, unverified fixture.

4. A protected operation needs a complete decision, not a button click

Before any protected commit, the authority owner must validate the exact principal, familiar root/revision, operation, target, input commitment, expected state revision, applicable lease generation, bounded parameters, authorization lifetime, and revocation state. Bind the final verification and commit atomically or to the same immutable snapshot. A preview or preflight result may become stale before the user confirms.

Prefer the established outcomes Permit / Degrade to Proposal / Reject. A UI may collect an intent while offline; it must not render a queued file as an accepted proposal or committed action. Creating the authoritative proposal itself may require authenticated submission. Proposal edits need new revision bindings so an approval cannot apply to different bytes.

The command-intent example (../../examples/proposed-command-intent.json) is a draft fixture, not an endpoint payload. It omits credentials and client-asserted authority. Its operation name and precondition names must be replaced by mapped canonical SDK types before any implementation uses them.

5. Submission, idempotency, and an unknown outcome

The client should establish a stable request identity before its first submission and preserve the exact intent bytes for retries. The server must bind any deduplication key to principal, operation, target and request content according to the canonical contract. Reusing the key with different content must fail explicitly; silently choosing one version is not acceptable. A client-generated key alone does not establish server deduplication, and server deduplication alone does not guarantee exactly-once effects at an external provider.

If a connection drops after submission, show outcome unknown. First query the authoritative operation/receipt status through the supported protocol. If committed, adopt that receipt. If rejected, display the rejection. If pending, keep it pending. If absence can be established under the protocol’s consistency and retention rules, follow its permitted retry path using the same identity and immutable request. Otherwise preserve uncertainty and surface an operator recovery action. Do not invent a new key to escape a pending request.

For an HTTP transport, RFC 9110 defines conditional requests such as If-Match and distinguishes idempotent methods from operations whose retries require additional knowledge. These are useful transport primitives, not substitutes for Coven’s operation authorization or external-effect reconciliation. An ETag only works as a concurrency precondition when the server defines and checks the relevant representation before mutation. HTTP source; retry semantics.

6. Attempts, leases, and cancellation

Every runtime attempt must carry its authoritative attempt identity and fencing context. The receiving authority verifies that context before accepting outputs or transitions. Lease expiry, transfer, cancellation, or recovery cannot be enforced solely by hoping an old process exits. A stale process may still produce bytes; those bytes must remain uncommitted until accepted under the current canonical rules.

Cancellation has at least two distinguishable observations: the request was accepted, and the attempt reached a terminal cancelled/stopped outcome. A disconnected view must not claim the second based on the first. Document whether children, remote provider requests, temporary files, and external side effects are cancellable, recoverable, or require reconciliation. Do not promise that cancellation reverses a provider-accepted action.

Retries require a classified failure, bounded policy, valid identity and current authority. A previous approval is not an unlimited retry capability. A paused mission, revoked familiar, changed input, expired authorization, or transferred lease must not be resumed by the UI’s retry button without the applicable canonical transition.

7. Host-folder and synchronization boundaries

Treat synchronized files as inputs, proposals, immutable artifacts, exports, or derived views according to an explicit allowlist. Do not synchronize live daemon databases, credentials, sockets, lock files, process handles, or host-specific lease ownership as ordinary project files. Do not turn receipt copies into writable authority records.

If Coven uses SQLite in the target implementation, its WAL is part of persistent database state; copying a live main database independently is not a safe synchronization design. SQLite documents database-aware snapshot mechanisms such as its Online Backup API. Use the established Coven export/backup owner and verify restore behavior rather than introducing a UI-controlled database-copy routine. WAL source; backup source.

An import must validate its destination root, normalized relative paths, archive traversal, symlinks, file types, size/resource limits and content commitments using host-appropriate primitives. Recheck at the actual write boundary; checking a path and later following a replaced symlink is insufficient. Unknown file types stay quarantined or excluded until their handling is defined. A manifest hash establishes byte identity, not authorization or trust in its producer.

Use explicit conflict objects or proposals for concurrent edits. Do not resolve familiar identity, authority records, accepted mission state, lease ownership, or approvals by timestamp or last-writer-wins. Remote ownership transfer is a canonical operation, not a folder move. Preserve unacknowledged local edits during reconciliation without treating them as accepted remote state.

8. Inputs, outputs, and privacy

Task text, repository instructions, model output, imported files and tool results are untrusted data. They may request a broader operation but cannot authorize it. Avoid wiring rendered prose or arbitrary file metadata directly into command construction. Validate operation variants and structured arguments in the canonical service, with output encoding and bounded rendering in the UI.

Keep credentials outside the shared Host tree and browser storage. Presentation preferences may remain local; authorization state must follow the supported credential/session mechanism. Logs and exported evidence should identify target, attempt, familiar revision, receipt and content commitment while redacting secrets and minimizing unnecessary prompt/file content. Retention and export policies require explicit product decisions before a real pilot.

The supplied presentation tests (../../tests/presentation.test.cjs) establish selected view logic and seal geometry. They do not prove identity enforcement, transport isolation, durable authorization, runtime containment, packaged behavior, revocation, or safe remote execution. The production acceptance matrix belongs in validation and acceptance, with evidence from the actual daemon, packaged clients and target runtime.

References and evidence status

  • Normative constraints supplied by Val: OpenCoven ownership boundaries and core laws in the task’s AGENTS.md instructions. These are requirements, not verified implementation findings.

  • Implemented prototype evidence: README, simulation and renderer, presentation fixtures (../../tests/presentation.test.cjs).

  • Primary technical references, checked 2026-11-18: SQLite WAL and Online Backup API; IETF RFC 9110 §§9.2.2 and 13.1.1, linked above. These substantiate limited technical guidance; they do not certify Coven’s current behavior.

The v3 references below identify a historical baseline. Pin the actual delivered source separately using its manifest/revision. The scalable layout/crown refinement is combined with replay/adaptive-mobile changes: run node scripts/verify-all.mjs for the suite, crown, static source, clean-extraction, rebuilding, and package checks; current counts are in tests/evidence/current.json. docs/handoff/11-open-decisions.md

Open decisions and proposal register

Status: recommendations for implementation discovery and owner review. This handoff does not establish new canonical APIs, repository ownership, authorization policy, or production readiness. The current Site is the working visual simulation described in README. Use architecture and ownership and implementation plan to turn these decisions into bounded engineering work.

Decisions that can proceed as reversible implementation work

During a separately assigned implementation task, the team can inspect repositories, map existing contracts, create isolated adapters and fixtures, prepare draft issues/PRs, and gather evidence within that task's authorization. This handoff request itself covers the source package, documentation, and Site download surface; it does not dispatch the proposed production work. Once implementation is assigned, carry authorized work far enough to make a policy choice concrete instead of stopping at a generic approval note.

Record a decision as proposed, accepted by owner, implemented, and verified separately. A checked-in proposal is not an owner decision; a merged patch is not proof of packaged or remote behavior. Superseded proposals remain linked to the decision that replaced them.

Decision register

The visual enclosure is a Project, using Coven's existing project noun. Castle definition decided by Val on 2026-11-19: a Castle is a bounded, hosted place where a Project's work runs and its results come back, with exactly one execution owner. OpenCoven/coven-host provides a Castle's folder surface (Castles/<name>/files in, results out); OpenCoven/coven-castles checks whether a sandbox is fit to back a Castle. A Project has zero or more Castles. A Castle is never the Project: its folder path and castle.json must not become a Project identity, and it keeps its own ID. Recommended dependency order

Resolve D01–D04 through repository discovery and a read-only adapter first. Those decisions make the nouns and read path concrete without changing authority. Prepare D05–D09 as a single vertical operation: one bounded mission, one attempt, one decision, one terminal receipt, including interrupted submission and cancellation. Then exercise D10 through a small synchronized artifact set, not the entire Host directory. Evaluate D11 with real canonical sample records before committing to visual metric claims. D12 is the pilot acceptance decision once the earlier evidence exists.

Discovery may show that several choices are already implemented and documented. In that case, record the exact contract/revision and adopt it; do not reopen the decision or fork its schema merely because this packet uses different provisional field names.

Decision packet template

Each decision packet should identify:

  1. The user problem, canonical component owner, and exact checked-out revisions.

  2. Existing implementation and normative contract evidence, including contrary evidence and unknowns.

  3. The smallest proposed change and at least one viable alternative where policy differs.

  4. Effects on identity, authority, persistence, compatibility, cancellation/recovery and user-visible state.

  5. The test or experiment that distinguishes the alternatives, its actual result, and its limits.

  6. The concrete action requiring acceptance, who can accept it, and how the record will remain auditable.

If a decision cannot be completed safely, preserve the work in a draft proposal with the blocked boundary identified. Continue independent read-only or reversible work. Do not relabel an unknown as “supported,” omit a failed check, weaken a gate, or auto-select a policy merely to finish the integration.

Exit criteria for closing this register

Close a decision only when its owner and outcome are recorded and linked to the canonical implementation or approved design. Close its implementation work only when the relevant tests pass. Close its delivery acceptance only when the packaged or hosted surface has been exercised at the pinned revision. Keep those records separate enough that a later regression can reopen the right part without erasing the original rationale.

The 2026-11-18 handoff-edition counts are in chapter 01

How the sources shape the proposal

The architectural boundary comes from S1: Coven owns authoritative transitions/persistence, Psyche owns orchestration semantics, Threads governs protected surfaces, and clients consume canonical SDK bindings. The source in S2–S4 provides a view and a local reducer that can be reused as a demonstration/fixture; it does not establish a production integration. The recommended first slice is therefore a verified read-only projection before operational commands.

S7–S8 support avoiding generic synchronization of a live database file. The proposed Host folder carries portable project inputs, approved immutable artifacts, and derived views; an authoritative daemon must own export/import and reconciliation. The exact current database, supported export mechanism, and platform recovery behavior remain discovery tasks.

S9 supports distinguishing transport retry behavior and conditional mutation checks. The proposed implementation additionally needs canonical receipt lookup, operation-specific authorization, revocation, idempotency retention, and external-effect reconciliation. Those requirements are design inferences and owner constraints, not features established by the RFC or this prototype.

S10's source fingerprints identify the historical mobile-matrix commit 9c7be88ca6797ef45a95764e2944653a399ee5c4 and handoff merge checkpoint 8eb108515b45a22bef5826fe2d4888845bace63a. S13 has a separate fingerprint set for the incoming replay/mobile source. Preserve both records as historical; neither establishes that S11 was browser-tested. JSON audits remain in the handoff, while historical browser screenshots are preserved in the repository only and excluded from the export. Headless Chromium QA of the current source ran on 2026-11-19 (record (../../tests/evidence/browser-qa-2026-11-19.json), summarized in chapter 01); it does not establish Safari, physical-device, real multi-touch, keyboard-only, or screen-reader acceptance. The current manifest identifies exported bytes, and chapter 01 records current checks; neither substitutes for fresh browser acceptance.

Historical material reviewed as context

The supplied local RFC titled “Refactoring Local IPC Socket Routing and PTY Process Supervision Across Coven and Psyche Subsystems” and the 30 October 2026 Cave iPhone Duo handoff were consulted for context. They include historical paths, commands, implementation assertions, or blocked checkpoints. This handoff does not import their exact APIs, version claims, limits, or platform statuses as current facts.

The older iPhone handoff is especially a reminder to inspect the current native product contract before adding destinations. The proposal here does not authorize restoration of retired Cave navigation or an unrelated native redesign.

Broader strategy files mentioned in older conversation memory were not supplied or freshly resolved in this task and were not treated as authoritative evidence. The first discovery packet must reconcile current roadmap, ADR, issue, PR, and repository instructions.

Production repository discovery

The owner named Coven Host, Coven Castles, Coven CLI, Psyche, and Psyche Build. On 2026-11-19 the map was renamed Coven Compass, and “Castle” now means a hosted execution place inside a Project (D01). Candidate repository names in the implementation documents are discovery starting points. Record exact repository URL, checkout, branch, revision, instructions, schemas, SDK symbols, and tests before using any binding. A product name is not proof of a dedicated repository or permission to create one.

No production API endpoint or CLI subcommand is asserted merely because it appears in a conceptual example. If a current canonical owner already implements a needed behavior, extend or consume it. If a responsibility is absent, record the gap and proposed owner for review instead of creating a duplicate control plane inside Compass.

docs/handoff/15-scalable-atlas-layout.md

Scalable Atlas layout and dimensional crown

Status: implemented; combined source-level verification passed. This user-requested refinement makes the Coven overview work with a changing number of projects and missions while preserving the existing visual language, and incorporates the adaptive mobile workspace and shared local replay clock. Browser, physical-device, and performance acceptance remain unverified; combined clean-extraction, rebuilding, and package verification passed. The refinement supplies presentation and local simulation behavior; it does not connect the Site to a Coven daemon or establish production readiness.

The inspected implementation surfaces are atlas-layout.js, atlas-viewport.js, atlas-crown.js, and the surrounding scene and UI adapter. These presentation helpers remain separate from authoritative orchestration state. This guide supersedes earlier overview positioning and zoom-driven scope assumptions. Read it alongside the visual contract, ownership map, and security and authority requirements.

1. What the geometry means

RepresentationMeaningConstraint
Castle courtyardOne project within the displayed Coven scopeCorner towers and curtain walls frame the Project. Openings align with route gates.
Mission count inside a ProjectExact known mission total in that ProjectEnter the Project or use the searchable mission browser for individual seals and details.
Central canonical crownPsyche coordination in the displayed scopeIts relief does not encode priority, progress, authority, or a separate identity.
Shared branch corridorA readable coordination connection from Psyche to a projectShared segments do not assert execution order, dependencies, network connectivity, or shared permissions.
Inward-facing Project gateWhere that project's coordination route meets its enclosureThe direction is geometric. North, east, south, and west do not create authorization categories.
Position in the latticeA stable presentation slotNearness to Psyche does not imply importance, ownership, scheduling priority, or stronger authority.

All overview Projects use the same enclosure vocabulary, including the currently selected project. Selecting a project elsewhere must not unexpectedly substitute its full internal scene into the overview. Familiar colors and glyphs retain their existing identity-recognition role; selection and urgency remain separate signals. Exact familiar roots and revisions belong to the verified data binding, never to color or shape. Visual contract

2. Compact placement for a changing project count

The layout helper accepts an ordered collection of unique project keys. It reserves a central hub and fills nearby lattice cells in opposite pairs. This produces a compact arrangement with balanced space around Psyche, including when the project count is odd. It avoids enlarging a single ring every time a project is added. The usable aspect ratio influences which nearby cells are selected: a wide canvas favors horizontal space, while a narrow canvas makes greater use of vertical space. Layout source

The Coven is drawn as a kingdom of Project castles. Plan and orbit project the same courtyard, curtain walls and towers. The footprint is shared across the overview, with roof and battlement detail revealed at larger scales. This architectural metaphor represents Project scope. Hosted Castle records retain their separate meaning in D01. Inside a Project the boundary can grow additional sides as missions accumulate. Psyche occupies a circular coordination disc with the upright crown in both scopes. Routes meet the overview disc at its edge. Plan view shows the face alone, and orbit reveals a shallow base proportional to its radius.

Each cell reserves the complete Project-and-label rectangle, not just the outline. The gaps between those rectangles are routing corridors. Routes leave the hub boundary, share suitable corridor segments, and make their final approach through the destination's inward-facing cardinal gate. A route may enter its own destination rectangle; it must not pass through another project's reserved space. The renderer must respect the helper's maxCornerRadius when rounding a branch, because excessive rounding can consume the reserved clearance.

At unchanged geometric options, appending keys preserves existing node positions. That guarantee depends on preserving caller order. Reordering keys, inserting an item earlier in the order, changing the available aspect ratio, or changing reserved dimensions can legitimately produce a different layout. Keep a stable project ordering at the adapter boundary; do not sort on rapidly changing agent counts or progress every frame. Filtering should retain spatial context where practical, and a change of project membership must remain distinguishable from a presentation rearrangement.

“N-many” means that placement is data-driven and has no hardcoded four-project or sixteen-project scenario. It does not promise unlimited rendering performance. Finite geometry, DOM cost, text legibility, interaction targets, and device limits still constrain useful detail. At dense counts, favor compact summaries, search, and project drilldown. Introducing viewport culling or list virtualization later requires measured evidence and must preserve the full accessible collection; it is not established by this geometry helper alone.

The overview uses a single count per Project. Project names appear when the projected enclosure is wide enough and remain available to assistive technology, the Projects drawer, and hover or focus. Density uses separate entry and exit thresholds to reduce flicker during zoom. At compact sizes, the boundary square marks a pending decision and the Project label and drawer provide the exact count. The larger badge has its own review target when there is room.

Explore larger Covens without removing user projects

The Projects drawer provides project-name search and Try a larger Coven presets for 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128 Projects. Presets add or remove only generated layout samples to approach the requested total. Existing baseline and user-created Projects are preserved; if that existing collection is already larger than a preset, the actual total remains larger. Remove extra samples removes only entries marked layoutDemo, rather than resetting the user's project collection. These are local simulation controls, not operations on external projects.

The former cosmetic sixteen-Project and twelve-mission creation caps have been removed. Mission resource bounds and protected decision/brief rules retain their separate semantics; removal of presentation creation caps grants no additional authority. The eight-seal overview cap still bounds presentation, and the supplied 128-Project preset remains a composition example rather than a system capacity limit or performance result. Sample controls and implementation

3. Eight seals, an honest remainder, and the full collection

missionPacking(count, options) supplies a bounded overview arrangement: up to eight seal slots and, when needed, one additional overflow slot. It returns total, visible, hidden, the visible positions, the overflow position/count, and a suitable seal radius. The helper does not change mission priority, state, progress, or the source collection. Caller order determines which missions occupy the visible slots. Packing implementation

A Project with thirteen known missions shows thirteen in its enclosure. Enter the Project for individual seals or use the searchable mission browser to open a mission directly.

Keep the complete known Project total separate from the number matching an active filter. Preserve the independent wedge and working-pip limits, with exact values in the mission details. Seal limits

The prototype can calculate exact totals from its complete in-memory fixtures. A production adapter may receive a partial page or unavailable count. In that case, retain coverage and freshness information and show an unknown or qualified total. Do not calculate an apparently complete +N from an incomplete page, and do not turn unavailable missions into a zero-mission dormant Project. Search and drilldown give access to the known collection. Show its coverage separately.

4. Scope and camera are separate controls

The interface needs an explicit Coven scope and an explicit project scope. Scope determines the collection, relationships, navigation context, and available details. Camera zoom determines how large that chosen scope appears. A zoom threshold must not silently change one scope into the other.

Opening a Project is a scope-navigation action. Returning to Coven is another. Panning, zooming, rotating, or tilting remains camera manipulation within the selected scope. Keep the active scope visible in navigation and preserve a predictable route back to the overview. Search results should carry their project identity so opening a result can establish scope deliberately.

Maintain an explicit auto-fit mode rather than inferring it from the current zoom factor. Initial entry and an intentional Fit action may enable auto-fit. A manual camera adjustment should preserve the user's framing. A resize may refit the scene only while auto-fit is active; it must not reset a manually chosen camera simply because a drawer, inspector, or viewport changed size. If an explicit scope change establishes a new framing, make that navigation behavior consistent and test it separately from resize handling.

The Coven overview defaults to 24° shallow relief, with overview orbit capped at 45°; project detail may reach 78°. These bounds retain clearance for the screen-facing crown and name. Fit includes explicit crown and label bounds rather than treating the compressed ground plane as the entire composition. The crown has no autonomous spinning or animation; changes reflect the chosen view.

Measure the usable canvas

Fit the projected content into the area actually available after visible chrome is accounted for. This includes the header, bottom familiar controls, and any inspector or panel that occludes the scene. Use measured rectangles and label extents rather than assuming a fixed screen size or compensating with a global scale constant.

The world-coordinate layout bounds include reserved Project rectangles, routes, hub, and padding. The camera layer additionally owns projection, screen-space labels, and chrome-safe insets. A label that remains fixed in screen pixels cannot be treated as if it always scales with the world. Reserve its measured space when fitting, and recompute when relevant typography or visible chrome changes. Handle a temporarily zero-sized viewport without generating invalid camera coordinates.

Use resize observation to update available dimensions, then apply the auto-fit policy. Coalesce repeated measurement changes into one presentation update. Preserve manual framing and avoid a measurement loop in which changing the camera repeatedly changes the dimensions being measured. This is presentation state; it must never write orchestration or identity state.

Adaptive workspace, keyboard, and replay integration

The mobile dock moves the existing replay and camera controls into Map, Missions, Activity, and View surfaces. Reusing those DOM nodes preserves their event handlers, draft/control state, and single replay owner. Compact, short-landscape, and tablet arrangements derive stage height from the visible viewport and measured header/dock space. Returning to desktop restores the controls to their existing positions. Mobile implementation

Update the lead-card structure before a queued fit measures it. Crossing the compact breakpoint can replace a manifest with a nested mobile HUD, so fitting against the previous structure produces incorrect safe space. Reserve the rendered HUD where it actually sits, and exclude CSS-hidden, DOM-hidden, or non-rendered chrome. A full mobile modal inspector obscures an inert map and is excluded from canvas-fit reservations; ordinary visible nonmodal inspector space still participates. The existing camera-dock and familiar-control observers cover popup closure and other size notifications without introducing a separate observer or camera owner.

Keyboard state is checked both when viewport changes arrive and inside the queued fit callback. A callback queued before the keyboard opens must not reframe the map while the user types. After it closes, automatic fitting resumes only if auto-fit remains enabled and the camera is unlocked. A manual camera adjustment continues to suppress incidental resize fitting.

The shared live replay cursor is separate from the camera. Project focus preserves playback time and playing/paused state; imported recordings retain their own extent and finish paused. Event-driven refreshes preserve elapsed replay time while camera smoothing uses its own bounded delta. All visible live Projects seek the shared cursor, and delayed reports remain in the trace without advancing replay prematurely. This is local demonstration playback, not authoritative execution time or a daemon event log.

When replay removes a selected mission, selection reconciliation restores the saved camera position and its saved auto-fit policy. Restoring zoom/pan alone would allow a later resize to erase the user's manual framing. Keep this cleanup distinct from an explicit Fit or scope-navigation action. The combined regression suite covers these interaction boundaries through source functions and DOM facades; browser rendering and physical keyboard behavior remain separate acceptance work. Scene and replay integration · Integration tests (../../tests/atlas-integration.test.cjs)

5. One canonical crown with restrained depth

The scene, header, key and conversation use the same faceted Psyche crown. Its inset section projects along a fourth coordinate to three quarters of the outer section. The connecting facets are clipped to the original crown silhouette. The scene adds a shallow rear face using the same silhouette. Derived edge samples form the extrusion's side walls, including the central aperture. The canonical path remains the identity-bearing asset; the sampled geometry is a rendering aid, not an alternative logo. Its provenance is recorded in the renderer and guarded by the dedicated crown check. Renderer · Crown check (../../scripts/test-atlas-crown.mjs)

Both map centers use the same lavender as the flat Psyche marks. A single darker lavender rim adds shallow, proportional depth along the bottom. The face stays upright as the camera orbits, preserving the canonical proportions and aperture. The tetrahedron familiar also keeps its upright portrait and level base in orbit and in the familiar editor. The rim is decorative, while mission-seal relief represents progress.

The integration interface is:

const crown = window.CovenAtlasCrown.create(psycheGroup, svgEl);
window.CovenAtlasCrown.draw(crown, {
  x: projectedX,
  y: projectedY,
  size: nominalWidth
});

Load the renderer before creating the scene crown. Coordinates are already projected SVG coordinates; size is the nominal full width in the same units. Keep the existing group's hit target and accessible Psyche label. The crown's own group is decorative and ignores pointer events. Reuse its record on redraw instead of rebuilding SVG nodes. Apply the same renderer at the Coven center and the project center; scale alone must not change what the crown means.

Map materials

Project courtyards use staggered flagstones. Paving follows the ground plane through orbit, and masonry joints follow the projected tower and wall faces. Fine paving and path borders drop out when projected courses become too small to resolve. The shapes and colors of decision markers, working agents and mission states carry their own meanings at every scale.

Psyche’s mount and mission seals use a graphite metal finish. Familiar faces and cog hubs retain their identity colors. An engraved groove follows each detailed seal wedge inside the separate resource rim. Seal Lab uses the same geometry as the map, and small inline seals use a single bevel around the face.

6. Integrate through existing owners

The following boundaries are supplied architecture requirements, not claims that production repositories have been inspected or integrated. Canonical ownership

ComponentIntegration responsibility
Coven HostPresent the existing workspace/project arrangement and discover its canonical bindings. Folder location and synced files do not create daemon authority.
CovenRetain daemon authority, durable state, sessions, runtime execution, and authoritative transitions. A layout snapshot is never a writable substitute.
PsycheSupply canonical task, lane, lease, approval, receipt, retry, and recovery semantics. Visual routes do not add dependency edges to that model.
Coven CompassDerive the human-readable scope, geometry, summaries, selection, and navigation from authorized projections. Keep camera and layout state local to presentation.
CaveReuse the presentation adapter and geometry where appropriate, while preserving production oversight, accessibility, freshness, and decision behavior.
Psyche BuildReuse the same canonical projection mapping for coding missions and lanes. Do not introduce a separate scheduler or approval implementation to support this map.
Coven CLIQuery and request actions through existing canonical bindings. Do not create a second persistence store or control plane to synchronize with the visualization.
SDK / Brand / UIProvide existing public bindings, approved identity assets/tokens, and reusable presentation specimens within their established ownership.

Before connecting live data, inspect the owning repositories and map their existing identifiers and state fields. Keep that mapping in a constrained presentation adapter rather than declaring this Site's fixture objects a new canonical schema. Familiars remain bound to an exact authorized root and revision. Pending decisions remain pending; a gate marker, route, selected Project, or crown never grants permission to commit a protected operation. Connection, freshness, and availability remain separate from mission lifecycle state. Authority requirements

7. Implementation sequence and execution tips

  1. Preserve stable inputs. Resolve project keys, caller order, complete or qualified totals, familiar bindings, and scope through the existing adapter. Keep operational state out of geometry functions.

  2. Compute one layout snapshot. Call CovenAtlasLayout.layout(keys, options) with measured available aspect and reserved Project/label dimensions. Cache by ordered keys and normalized geometric options, not by every mission-progress tick.

  3. Render one overview vocabulary. Use the uniform four-corner Project for each project. Place routes from the returned points and gate metadata, respecting corridor clearance and maximum corner radius.

  4. Bound map detail. Show Project totals on the overview. Use projected scale and spacing to reveal seal relief and selected agents within the Project. Preserve the selected mission and keep the full collection accessible through the mission browser.

  5. Keep scope explicit. Connect project opening, Coven return, and search results to navigation. Connect Fit and camera gestures to camera state. Avoid zoom-based scope switching.

  6. Fit the measured safe area. Include projected geometry and screen-space labels, observe relevant chrome changes, and refit on resize only in auto-fit mode.

  7. Reuse the crown record. Keep canonical front faces and decorative relief isolated from flat UI marks, hit targets, and semantic mission topography.

  8. Record integrated evidence. Validate source geometry first, then the actual browser interaction and packaged artifact. A source-only pass does not qualify live data, touch behavior, or production authority.

8. Verification scope and remaining acceptance

Combined source-level result: node scripts/verify-all.mjs runs the suite, the crown check (canonical digest, aperture, bounds, stable nodes, and every view/size combination), the static source checker, and a clean-extraction rebuild and archive verification. It records the current counts in tests/evidence/current.json (../../tests/evidence/current.json). The earlier layout-branch extraction/rebuild remains historical evidence in chapter 01, not verification of this combined ZIP. Source success does not establish browser acceptance.

The layout test sweep covers selected project counts 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 64, and 128 and geometric invariants. Mission-packing integration covers every integer count from 0 through 128. This is a bounded source-level correctness range, not a load test, production benchmark, browser frame-rate claim, or maximum supported project count. The crown check covers canonical-path provenance, finite geometry, preserved aperture, bounded footprint, and record reuse. Refer to the tests for their precise cases. Layout tests (../../tests/atlas-layout.test.cjs) · Crown check (../../scripts/test-atlas-crown.mjs)

Relevant focused commands are:

node --test tests/atlas-layout.test.cjs
node scripts/test-atlas-crown.mjs
node scripts/check-source.mjs

Headless Chromium QA of the current source ran on 2026-11-19 (record (../../tests/evidence/browser-qa-2026-11-19.json), summarized in chapter 01); it does not establish Safari, physical-device, real multi-touch, keyboard-only, or screen-reader acceptance. Before calling the integrated result visually accepted, inspect desktop and narrow layouts with chrome open and closed; zero, one, odd, and dense project counts; more than eight missions; exact overflow and aggregate totals; density transitions; project/mission search and drilldown; sample presets and preservation of user-created Projects on reset; keyboard and touch navigation; label overlap; route clearance; explicit scope changes; auto-fit resize behavior; and preservation of a manually adjusted camera. Check the canonical aperture and readable depth at low pitch in both scopes.

Browser QA should cover desktop and narrow layouts in both camera modes. Check dense sample presets, exact Project totals, selection and focus across density changes, label and leader clearance, and the shared seal geometry in Seal Lab.

Older screenshots or unrelated mobile checks do not establish acceptance of this refinement. No daemon integration, live authorization behavior, production throughput, or cross-device persistence is demonstrated by these presentation tests. Use the existing validation plan and evidence record template for the integration's remaining gates.

Locally generated SVG specimens illustrate the source geometry only. They are not browser screenshots, interactive QA, or device-performance evidence.

docs/handoff/source-context/user-architecture-instructions.md

Owner-supplied architecture constraints

Source: Val's instructions supplied in this conversation on 18 November 2026. These are design and engineering requirements for this handoff, not independently verified claims about current repository implementation. Personal profile information and unrelated instructions are excluded.

Canonical ownership

  • Familiar Contract: governed portable familiar identity.

  • SPAR: continuity profile/query plane explaining continuity across revisions, runtimes, sessions, devices, models, memories, and embodiments. It is not a second identity root or competing database.

  • Coven Threads: protected-surface authorization and proposal-versus-commit decisions.

  • Psyche: orchestration semantics, including tasks, lanes, leases, approvals, receipts, retries, and recovery.

  • Coven: daemon authority, persistence, sessions, runtime execution, and authoritative state transitions.

  • Coven Runtimes: runtime capability descriptors and conformance.

  • SDK: constrained public clients and canonical bindings.

  • Coven Memory: read-only memory client/projection, never a second memory authority.

  • Cave: primary human oversight product and production UI behavior.

  • Psyche Build: multi-lane coding cockpit consuming Psyche canonically.

  • Coven Code: terminal coding execution.

  • Coven GitHub: GitHub-triggered familiar delivery.

  • Brand: canonical visual identity and voice.

  • UI: specimen/component laboratory, not production authority.

Core laws

  • Identity precedes work. Identity, intent, authority, orchestration, and execution remain separate.

  • No UI, prompt, model response, task text, or caller-supplied field may grant itself protected authority.

  • Authoritative objects gate writes; derived views provide legibility. Clients are untrusted for enforcement.

  • Familiar sessions bind to an exact authorized familiar root and revision.

  • Protected changes require authenticated principal authority, operation-specific authorization, replay protection, revocation/recovery semantics, and auditable receipts.

  • Final authorization verification and commit must be atomic or use the same immutable snapshot.

  • Pending proposals must never appear as committed state.

  • Stale, degraded, reconciling, disconnected, rejected, and unavailable are explicit states.

  • Prefer Permit / Degrade to Proposal / Reject.

  • Fail closed at identity, authorization, persistence, release, and publication boundaries.

  • Structural conformance alone does not establish security, privacy, safety, personhood, or legal ownership.

  • Familiars are AI systems. Product language may be evocative; normative claims remain technically honest.

  • Cloud infrastructure is an execution surface, not the fundamental home of identity.

  • Before introducing a repository, service, schema, database, control plane, or abstraction, check whether an existing canonical component owns the responsibility.

  • Prefer fewer coherent systems over overlapping ones.

Engineering and decision rules

Inspect current repository state, relevant scoped instructions, README/ADRs/schemas/tests/CI, issue and PR context, and branch/worktree constraints first. Preserve unrelated work and respect archived, read-only, reference-only, or intentionally dirty worktrees. Trace authority and data flow before changing behavior; fix the invariant with the smallest safe patch.

Do not weaken security, ownership, release, conformance, or evidence gates to make tests pass. Add red-to-green evidence for bugs and authority boundaries. Run the narrowest relevant tests before broader gates, and use real-daemon or packaged-artifact checks when source-only tests can conceal failure. Report exact commands, revisions, results, skipped checks, remaining uncertainty, and risks.

Current explicit owner instructions and current implementation evidence outrank older planning notes. Distinguish implemented, verified, specified, approved design, proposed, experimental, deprecated, and unknown/unverified. Obtain the authorization required for consequential actions; creating this handoff does not authorize production deployment, credential changes, merging, or external communications in another repository.

docs/handoff/templates/acceptance-checklist.md

Acceptance checklist — template

Use for a real implementation candidate. Check a box only when evidence for the current source/package revision exists.

Contract and ownership

  • [ ] Current repository revisions and scoped instructions recorded.

  • [ ] Existing canonical schemas/SDK symbols mapped; no competing authority store introduced.

  • [ ] Exact principal and familiar root/revision bindings verified.

  • [ ] Read-only, proposal, and committed mutation paths are distinguishable.

Projection and UI

  • [ ] Complete, partial, stale, disconnected, degraded, reconciling, and unavailable data tested.

  • [ ] Event gaps, duplicates, reconnect, and snapshot replacement reconcile correctly.

  • [ ] Shape/color/location meanings and exact-count details preserved.

  • [ ] Keyboard, touch, screen-reader, contrast, text scaling, and reduced-motion checks recorded.

Authority and execution

  • [ ] Operation-specific authorization and commit share the correct immutable inputs.

  • [ ] Revoked, expired, mismatched, replayed, and stale requests fail as specified.

  • [ ] Idempotency and lost-ack reconciliation prove bounded effects.

  • [ ] Lease/fencing, crash recovery, cancellation, resource limits, and runtime refusal exercised against the real owner.

  • [ ] Pending proposals and unknown outcomes never display as committed.

Host and portability

  • [ ] Portable files are classified and live databases/secrets/runtime state excluded from generic sync.

  • [ ] Conflicts, interrupted sync, changed authority owner, and disconnected execution tested.

  • [ ] A clean extracted artifact runs and its verification commands work without Git history.

  • [ ] Packaged CLI/native clients and remote-host evidence are recorded separately.

Delivery

  • [ ] Exact source and package receipts are attached.

  • [ ] Failures, skips, remaining decisions, and safe-disable behavior are explicit.

  • [ ] Required human/product acceptance recorded.

  • [ ] Release/publication/merge authorization and normal gates satisfied for the actual destination.

docs/handoff/templates/evidence-record.md

Evidence record — template

Identity of the check

  • Packet / issue / PR:

  • Repository and exact source commit:

  • Build/package identity and digest, if applicable:

  • Platform, architecture, tool versions:

  • Environment: fixture / source / real daemon / packaged CLI / native client / remote host / human acceptance

  • Start/end timestamp and timezone:

  • Executor and reviewer:

Claim under examination

State one claim and the source of its expected behavior. Specify whether the check verifies implementation, conformance, authorization, persistence, recovery, interoperability, or only presentation.

Reproduction

Exact commands, setup, inputs, and faults injected.
Use synthetic data. Do not include tokens, raw credentials, private memory, or personal conversations.

Result

  • Exit codes and pass/fail/skip counts:

  • Observed state before/after:

  • Canonical object revisions / lease or attempt identifiers:

  • Receipts or redacted trace references:

  • Expected refusal or failure evidence:

  • Artifact paths and hashes:

  • RED baseline and GREEN patched result, where applicable:

Limits

  • What this check does not establish:

  • Skipped checks and reasons:

  • Known failures / unknown commit outcomes:

  • Recovery performed:

  • Next acceptance check:

“Not run,” “blocked,” “failed,” and “unknown” are distinct outcomes. Preserve them. A claim becomes verified only at the scope the evidence actually exercises.

docs/handoff/templates/implementation-packet.md

Implementation packet — template

Goal and status

  • Packet ID / title:

  • User-visible outcome:

  • Current status: proposed / in progress / implemented / verified / blocked / ready for review

  • Owning component and repository:

  • Baseline revision / branch / isolated worktree:

  • Scoped instructions and canonical ADR/schema links:

  • Related issue/PR and dependencies:

Scope

Describe the smallest complete vertical slice. Identify the canonical behavior being consumed or changed, the adapter/client code involved, and explicit exclusions. Record whether this packet has read-only, proposal, or mutation behavior.

Identity and authority path

  • Principal/session source:
