README.md

Coven Compass

A private, interactive Site exploration of the supplied Coven Castles v27 prototype. This presentation builds on its existing event-driven simulation; it does not connect to a Coven daemon or confer protected authority.

Full source and implementation handoff

Open START_HERE.md for the runnable ZIP workflow and the handoff index for the complete proposed architecture, ownership, synchronization/recovery plan, execution packets, agent prompts, acceptance matrix, and evidence ledger. The in-app Handoff entry opens a readable guide and downloads the complete source package. The implementation proposal covers Coven Host, Compass, Coven CLI, Psyche, Psyche Build, SDK, Threads, Cave, familiar identity, runtimes, and read-only memory/continuity views.

The handoff preserves the prototype as a simulation. Production APIs, schemas, and command paths require current-repository discovery and acceptance; conceptual JSON examples are inert documentation fixtures.

Run every check with one command. CI runs the same command on every pull request (.github/workflows/verify.yml, repository only):

node scripts/verify-all.mjs

It runs the steps below, then repeats the source, test, crown, and manifest checks in a clean extraction of the built ZIP. It exits non-zero if any step fails or is skipped. When everything passes it writes the measured counts to tests/evidence/current.json (tests/evidence/current.json); commit that file with your change. CI runs --check, which fails if the file is stale.

node scripts/check-source.mjs
node --test tests/*.test.cjs
node scripts/test-atlas-crown.mjs
python3 scripts/build-handoff.py
python3 scripts/verify-handoff.py dist/downloads/Coven_Compass_Handoff_2026-11-19.zip

The tests include their exact reference fixture and work without Git history. The generated export includes the mobile-readiness report, source harness, historical JSON evidence, and its own inventory and checksums. Historical browser screenshots remain in the repository only and are excluded from the handoff, along with credentials, runtime data, and previous ZIPs. Historical fingerprints describe their recorded checkpoint; they are not verification of the current layout source.

Scalable overview refinement

Implemented; combined source-level verification passed. The current refinement uses castle courtyards for Projects in an aspect-aware compact lattice, paired positions, and shared branch corridors that meet each project's inward-facing gate. Routes show coordination, not execution dependencies or authority. Read the scalable layout and crown guide for implementation and integration details.

The Coven overview shows an exact mission count within each Project enclosure and a separate badge for pending decisions. The mission browser and Project drilldown retain all known missions. The map reduces detail based on projected spacing while preserving the underlying collection.

Open Projects → Try a larger Coven for 8, 16, 32, 64, or 128-Project sample presets. Remove extra samples removes only generated layout samples and preserves existing baseline and user-created Projects. A preset never reduces the user's existing collection to meet its target, so the actual total can exceed the requested preset. These samples explore composition; 128 is neither a production capacity claim nor an architectural limit.

Coven/project scope is explicit and separate from camera zoom. Fit uses measured chrome-safe space; resize refits only in auto-fit mode and preserves a manually adjusted camera. The canonical Psyche crown has restrained projected relief in both scene scopes, with its exact aperture and leaf silhouette. Flat UI marks remain unchanged; the sculpture does not spin or glow.

Visual language

  • Castle courtyard: one project's scope. Every project uses the same overview treatment, including the currently active project.

  • Circular mission seal: one mission. Wedge angle is the share of its agents led by each familiar; wedge height is progress on that familiar's role-owned targets; the central signet expresses mission state.

  • Stable familiar glyph and hue: identity across projects, councils, and delegated agents. Changing the camera angle does not change the familiar's mark.

  • Agent marks: cogs represent agents and square hubs indicate task assignments in the selected mission. Their state and familiar affiliation remain available in the detail views.

  • Near-white boundary square: a pending permission or resource-limit decision. Selecting it opens that project's pending decisions; its presence does not mean the requested operation was approved.

  • Central Psyche crown: coordination within the current scope. Its relief is decorative, while project connections remain neutral until a familiar filter highlights that familiar's assignments.

  • Coral seal rim: the tightest time, token, or budget limit has reached 85%, or the mission is broken after stopping at a limit.

The Coven overview shows Project boundaries, exact mission counts, and pending-decision badges. Entering a Project reveals mission seals and familiar glyphs. Selecting a mission shows its state, one decision preview, and individual agent marks when spacing allows. The Inbox holds all pending decisions, and mission details retain exact counts. Zoom changes presentation density while preserving the current scope.

The v27 seal constraints remain: a 12-degree minimum wedge angle, at most eight rendered council wedges, and at most twelve working pips per familiar. The minimum angle can enlarge very small shares; exact agent counts remain available in detail views.

Interactions

  1. Browse the Coven map or open Projects to search project names and explore the larger-Coven sample presets. Use Missions to search across Projects and filter by Project or mission state; an overview overflow marker opens all missions for its Project.

  2. Use the familiar chips along the bottom to follow a familiar across Projects. Select the same chip again to clear the filter.

  3. Select a near-white square on a project boundary to open its pending decisions.

  4. Open mission details for Brief, Council, Tasks, and Agents. Previous/Next explores the current Project; Back to mission leaves a familiar view; All missions restores the search and selected row.

  5. Use Seal lab to explore Planned, Active, Needs you, Stalled, Sealed, and Broken, plus target progress, working counts, and resource limits.

  6. Replay the shared live timeline, pause or scrub to a moment, and change the focused Project without restarting playback. Go live returns to the current sample state. Imported recordings keep their own extent and finish paused.

  7. On mobile, use Map, Missions, Activity, and View in the bottom workspace dock. Replay and Go live stay reachable while browsing the map; View reveals the 2D, 3D, Move, Orbit, zoom, Fit, and Lock controls. Drag to pan in 2D; choose Move or Orbit in 3D. Two-pointer pan/pinch preserves the point under the gesture centroid. Fit enables automatic framing; a manual camera adjustment preserves that framing through later resize events.

Mission routes include Project identity, mission, section, familiar scope, and card/detail mode. Browser Back/Forward and reload restore that state. A mission that disappears at an earlier replay position clears its selection with an explanatory status message.

Mobile sheets follow the visible viewport, keep the active surface above the map, and restore focus through nested views. Mission and Project forms keep their header/action row outside the scrolling fields. Draft text survives resizing and minimizing/reopening the conversation within the loaded session.

The mobile dock moves the original controls instead of creating a second replay state. It yields to open sheets and the keyboard, and restores the controls to their desktop positions when the layout changes. The available viewport and measured header/dock heights determine the map height. Compact, short-landscape, and tablet arrangements adapt to screen shape; an explicit View expansion survives rotation.

Replay renders missions before their first council seat, so opening events no longer stop the frame loop. Event refreshes preserve elapsed time, and camera smoothing retains its separate bounded delta. All visible Projects follow the shared replay cursor; delayed sample reports remain in the trace until that cursor reaches them.

The starting model contains four Projects, seven missions, and 114 delegated agents. All displayed totals are derived from the simulation. Activity changes over time. Chat and approval controls affect sample data only; they do not send communications, run agents, authorize real operations, or write to external projects.

Projection sources

The mode is explicit. With no source parameter the Site runs the simulation exactly as before. ?source=fixture (optionally &scenario=fresh|stale|partial|disconnected|unsupported-version) reads a static fixture shaped after Cave Client v1 projects.list, as cited in the D01–D04 discovery (docs/discovery/2026-11-19-d01-d04/README.md). It shows each Project's name, root, and Cave id separately, and labels the state explicitly as fresh, stale, reconciling (incomplete pages), or unavailable (disconnected, unsupported version, unreadable). Any non-simulation mode stops before the simulation boots, and an unknown source value shows unavailable, so sample data never stands in for another source. There is no live mode: D03 is unresolved.

Both sources implement one interface, read() → Promise<Projection>, described at the top of dist/projection-source.js. A live adapter would be a third implementation of that interface. In simulation mode the map still renders from its own state; the registered simulation source wraps atlasSnapshot for consumers of the interface.

Source

  • dist/index.html: original simulation and seal renderer, with scope-based scene visibility and the orchestration-atlas integration.

  • dist/atlas-ui.js, dist/atlas.css: navigation, searchable mission browser, responsive sheets, familiar filters, and touch camera controls.

  • dist/atlas-layout.js: compact paired project placement, corridor routing, bounds, and bounded overview mission packing.

  • dist/atlas-viewport.js: measured safe-area fitting for the projected scene and visible chrome.

  • dist/atlas-crown.js: exact canonical crown faces with sampled extrusion walls and restrained solid shading.

  • dist/mission-navigation.js: canonical route codec and replay selection reconciliation.

  • dist/projection-source.js, dist/fixtures/cave-projects-list.json: the projection seam and its static fixture (see Projection sources below).

  • dist/mobile-interactions.js: pointer geometry, camera gestures, and visual viewport geometry.

  • dist/mobile-ui.js: responsive portals, adaptive workspace dock, measured map space, modal stacking, focus restoration, keyboard handling, and viewport variables.

  • dist/semantic-map.css: scope-specific scene visibility, familiar glyphs, agent marks, and boundary decision markers.

  • dist/seal-lab.js, dist/seal-lab.css: an isolated visual explorer using the actual seal renderer.

  • tests/*.test.cjs: focused Node regression tests for layout, viewport geometry, routes, replay, focus, modal ownership, forms, gestures, and preserved seal geometry. Run the command above for the current count.

  • scripts/test-atlas-crown.mjs: canonical-path provenance, aperture, finite geometry, footprint, and SVG record-reuse checks.

  • Replay clock (tests/replay-clock.test.cjs), replay rendering (tests/replay-render.test.cjs), and delayed-report (tests/replay-emission.test.cjs) tests cover elapsed playback, project focus, shared bounds, early mission events, and delayed emission. Mobile UI (tests/mobile-ui.test.cjs) and mobile focus (tests/mobile-focus.test.cjs) tests cover the adaptive workspace and focus targets.

  • tests/mobile-qa.html: an interactive responsive QA harness, excluded from the deployment.

  • tests/evidence/: historical mobile and incoming replay/mobile JSON audits with source fingerprints; repository-only browser screenshots are excluded from the exported handoff.

  • MOBILE_READINESS.md: separate mobile, replay, and layout checkpoints, the combined source's verification boundary, and physical-device acceptance criteria.

No build step or runtime dependencies are required. Google Fonts is the inherited optional typography dependency, with system font fallbacks.

Verification and evidence boundary

Current counts are generated, not written by hand. node scripts/verify-all.mjs records the current test, crown, and package counts in tests/evidence/current.json (tests/evidence/current.json), and CI fails when that file is stale. Its evidence level is static + unit: Node fixtures with DOM facades, not a browser, device, daemon, packaged CLI, or remote Host.

The source integrates layout/crown work with replay and adaptive-mobile improvements from 07919b421df5457e778e1b1c6a73512c8f27ba73. Earlier checkpoints (the layout/crown branch, the incoming replay/adaptive-mobile branch with its Chrome audits, and the mobile/navigation baseline) are historical records with their own counts in current state and evidence and Mobile readiness. They do not verify the current source.

The incoming replay/mobile audit record (tests/evidence/replay-mobile-layout-audits.json) retains diagnostic failures separately from successful retests, source fingerprints, and interaction notes. It covers replay, the adaptive dock, mission surfaces, focus, and draft retention for that earlier source. Historical browser JPGs remain in the repository only, including tests/evidence/replay-mobile-320.jpg; they are excluded from the handoff. Mobile readiness preserves the detailed records without treating them as validation of this merge.

Layout geometry covers selected project counts through 128: 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 64, and 128. Mission-packing integration covers every integer count from 0 through 128. These source cases are not browser load or production benchmarks.

Headless Chromium QA of the current source ran on 2026-11-19 (record (tests/evidence/browser-qa-2026-11-19.json), summarized in chapter 01); it does not establish Safari, physical-device, real multi-touch, keyboard-only, or screen-reader acceptance. Incoming Chrome evidence does not remove that current limitation or verify the merged layout. Node fixtures use DOM facades and numeric inputs. Historical Chrome audits used a browser layout engine but did not establish Safari, a physical keyboard, real multi-touch, VoiceOver, or folding-hardware behavior. This remains a local visual simulation; production integration and device acceptance require separate evidence.

START_HERE.md

Coven Compass — full implementation handoff

Prepared for Val · 18 November 2026 · package edition 1

This package contains the complete runnable Compass source, its regression fixtures, a readable handoff, and a proposed integration plan for Coven Host, Coven Compass, Coven CLI, Psyche, Psyche Build, and related OpenCoven components.

The implemented application is a local simulation. The backend integration is a proposal. This handoff does not establish that a production repository implements a proposed API, folder layout, lease, receipt, or authorization behavior. Verify canonical contracts at current pinned revisions before implementation.

The scalable overview and crown refinement now incorporates adaptive-mobile replay improvements; combined source-level verification passed. It adds compact project placement, bounded overview mission detail, project search and sample presets, explicit scope, chrome-safe fit, and canonical crown relief. See guide 15; historical browser evidence does not qualify these changes.

Start in ten minutes

  1. Start at the root of your Git checkout. If you received the ZIP, extract it and work from the extracted Coven_Compass_Handoff_2026-11-19 directory.

  2. Read this file, then current state and evidence.

  3. For an extracted delivery, run python3 scripts/verify-handoff.py . before making edits. In a Git checkout, run node scripts/verify-all.mjs instead: the manifest and checksums are generated into the ZIP and aren't committed, so verify-handoff.py . refuses a checkout and says so.

  4. Preview Compass locally. Enter a Project, select a mission, inspect its agents and pending decisions, and try familiar filters and Seal lab. In Projects, use project search and Try a larger Coven to explore the 8/16/32/64/128 sample presets; Remove extra samples preserves baseline and user-created Projects. Start replay and switch Projects while it plays; on mobile, explore the Map, Missions, Activity, and View dock.

  5. Read architecture and ownership, then take the discovery packet in the implementation plan.

The handoff HTML is also available at dist/handoff/guide.html. Markdown chapters are the editable documentation source. The Site's Handoff entry links to the same package and reader.

The application in dist/ is editable browser source. The builder generates dist/handoff/guide.html and the downloadable archive. Preserve the baseline under tests/fixtures/ and dated audits under tests/evidence/ as historical evidence.

Run and check

From a Git checkout, run the full verification with node scripts/verify-all.mjs (sh scripts/verify-checkout.sh is the same command). It runs every check below plus the clean-extraction checks, and exits non-zero if any step fails or is skipped. See AGENTS.md (AGENTS.md) for editable sources and focused checks.

The package has no npm dependencies and needs no application build. Use Node.js 24 and Python 3.10 or newer; the tested runtimes are Node.js 24.22.1 and Python 3.12.14. Exact results are recorded in the evidence note. The bundled reference fixture makes the unit tests independent of Git history and network access.

node scripts/check-source.mjs
node --test tests/*.test.cjs
node scripts/test-atlas-crown.mjs
python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory dist

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ in your browser. Stop the local preview with Ctrl+C. These preview instructions are for the recipient's local development machine; a managed Sites environment should use its documented preview tooling.

Current results are generated: run node scripts/verify-all.mjs from a source checkout. It runs the source, unit, crown, build, ZIP, and clean-extraction checks and records the current counts in tests/evidence/current.json (tests/evidence/current.json). Historical checkpoints, including the earlier layout/crown branch, keep their own counts in current state and evidence.

The incoming replay/adaptive-mobile branch at 07919b421df5457e778e1b1c6a73512c8f27ba73 recorded its own Node and Chrome evidence before this combined layout. It adds a shared live replay timeline that preserves elapsed time and playing/paused state across project focus changes, while imported recordings keep their own extent. Delayed reports do not force replay to the live edge. Its adaptive workspace reuses the original controls; measured header/dock space and the visible viewport support compact, short-landscape, and tablet arrangements.

Read MOBILE_READINESS.md for the distinct incoming replay/mobile record, the older mobile baseline, and native-device limits. Neither record verifies the combined source. Headless Chromium QA of the current source ran on 2026-11-19 (record (tests/evidence/browser-qa-2026-11-19.json), summarized in chapter 01); it does not establish Safari, physical-device, real multi-touch, keyboard-only, or screen-reader acceptance. The current evidence note records the combined source and ZIP results, including the exact clean-extraction commands and inventory counts.

The checksum verifier validates the delivered snapshot. After intentionally editing files, changed checksums are expected; run the source/unit checks and rebuild the export. A checksum manifest detects byte changes relative to itself. It is not a cryptographic signature or a proof of trust.

python3 scripts/build-handoff.py
python3 scripts/verify-handoff.py dist/downloads/Coven_Compass_Handoff_2026-11-19.zip

To check the extracted delivery independently, run these commands from the checkout.

export_check=$(mktemp -d)
python3 -m zipfile -e dist/downloads/Coven_Compass_Handoff_2026-11-19.zip "$export_check"
python3 scripts/verify-handoff.py "$export_check/Coven_Compass_Handoff_2026-11-19"

The generated ZIP is excluded from its own contents. It can be recreated from the extracted package. The other files required to run Compass and rebuild the handoff are included.

Package map

  • dist/: complete static application plus the handoff landing page and generated reader.

  • docs/handoff/: architecture, integration proposal, folder synchronization, implementation plan, execution playbook, acceptance matrix, visual contract, scalable layout/crown guide, security, agent prompts, decisions, and sources.

  • docs/handoff/templates/: implementation packet, binding inventory, evidence record, and acceptance checklist.

  • tests/: source regression coverage for presentation/layout/viewport geometry, navigation, replay timing/rendering/delayed reports, adaptive mobile controls, gestures/overlays, and mission interactions; the pinned v2 reference source; and historical JSON evidence. Run the full command for the combined count. Replay cases are in clock (tests/replay-clock.test.cjs), render (tests/replay-render.test.cjs), and emission (tests/replay-emission.test.cjs) tests.

Git metadata, credentials, local runtime state, browser profiles, historical QA screenshots, installed dependencies, and previous export archives are intentionally excluded. No license or production authority is created by this package. Preserve the applicable upstream terms and current repository instructions when integrating.

First implementation recommendation

Deliver one read-only Project backed by the canonical Coven projection before enabling operational commands. Map a familiar's exact identity revision, one mission, its task/attempt state, a pending decision, and a resulting receipt into Compass. Show source freshness and disconnection explicitly. Then introduce bounded command proposals through the existing SDK/authorization path and prove refusal/recovery behavior before connecting remote execution.

Keep the simulation available as an explicit demo/fixture mode. A production mode must not silently fall back to sample data, synthetic acknowledgements, or browser-generated success states.

Publishing and reuse

The manifest identifies the existing private Site. It is provenance and configuration, not a publishing credential. Updating that Site requires authorized source access and its normal publish flow. A separate fork needs its own registered Site identity; never invent an ID or accidentally publish a fork over the original.

No production repositories were modified, no real agent was launched, and no production permissions were granted while preparing this handoff. The acceptance matrix defines what evidence is still needed before a real integration can be called ready.

Coven Compass mobile readiness

Mobile, replay, and layout checkpoints recorded November 18, 2026; combined-source verification tracked separately below.

Current status and historical boundary

Current source and package counts are generated by node scripts/verify-all.mjs into tests/evidence/current.json (tests/evidence/current.json) and checked by CI. Everything below is a dated record and is not updated with later changes.

At that checkpoint the final combined suite passed 207 tests with zero failures, cancellations, or skips; the crown check passed 84 view/size combinations plus canonical digest/aperture/bounds/stable-node checks; and the static source checker passed. Combined ZIP clean-extraction, rebuilding, and archive verification passed, including the same source suite and crown checks in the extracted copy. Headless Chromium QA of the current source ran on 2026-11-19 (record (tests/evidence/browser-qa-2026-11-19.json), summarized in chapter 01); it does not establish Safari, physical-device, real multi-touch, keyboard-only, or screen-reader acceptance. The incoming audit records its own source fingerprints; it is pre-this-combined-layout evidence, not a new browser run against the merged artifact. Current results belong in current state and evidence. Physical iPhone/Safari acceptance remains necessary for a production device claim. The Site remains a local simulation without a native iOS binary, daemon connection, persistent mission execution, or real authorization.

The overview retains compact paired placement, shared coordination corridors, and full/compact/tiny density modes. Full detail shows at most eight mission seals plus overflow; denser views show exact aggregates, with all missions available through search and drilldown. The Projects drawer provides project search and 8/16/32/64/128 sample presets; Remove extra samples preserves baseline and user-created Projects. Coven/project scope stays explicit. Measured stage changes from the adaptive dock must honor the same auto-fit policy: resize refits only in auto-fit mode and preserves manual framing. Scalable layout guide

The implementation adapts to viewport size and primary pointer type. It does not hard-code an iPhone model or assume that folding produces one particular CSS resolution. Mobile sheets apply through 1100 CSS pixels and on primary coarse-pointer devices.

Interaction contract

SurfaceExpected behavior
MissionsSearch mission, Project, or familiar; filter by Project and state; recover from no matches with Clear filters.
Detail explorationBrief, Council, Tasks, and Agents use accessible tabs. Arrow keys, Home, and End move between sections. Previous/Next stays within the Project.
Familiar scopeBack to mission returns to the whole selected mission.
Agent scopeSelecting an agent reveals and focuses its information. Close agent details returns to its row. Live updates keep the same focused controls.
Return to browsingAll missions retains the query, filters, scroll position, and selected mission.
Browser navigationRoutes identify Project and mission together, section, familiar, and card/detail mode. Back/Forward and reload restore this state; transient navigation drawers close during route restoration.
ReplayPlayback crosses mission opening and council-seating events. Project focus preserves playing/paused state and time. Live Projects share one timeline, including empty focused Projects; imported recordings keep their own extent and finish paused. A removed mission/familiar/agent is reconciled immediately.
Mobile workspaceMap, Missions, and Activity open existing surfaces. Replay and Go live remain reachable on the map. View expands the existing camera controls; Escape folds them without leaving the selected mission.
Adaptive viewsCompact, short-landscape, and tablet arrangements use visible viewport geometry and measured header/dock heights. Rotation retains an explicit camera expansion and the original control/draft nodes.
2D traversalA direct drag pans without changing the viewing plane.
3D traversalOrbit changes yaw/pitch; Move pans. Orbit has a six-degree lower bound so a downward drag does not strand the user in 2D mode. The 2D control deliberately selects the flat plane.
Two-pointer traversalPan and pinch are calculated together around the moving centroid. Adding/removing a pointer rebases the gesture rather than jumping.
Scope, Fit, and LockCoven/project scope is explicit and does not switch at a zoom threshold. Fit restores the current scope using measured chrome-safe space and enables auto-fit; resize preserves a manually adjusted camera. Lock disables the seven camera actions and direct map gestures; Unlock remains available.
Mobile overlaysOnly the top managed sheet is interactive. Tab wraps, Escape closes the top surface, and nested closes restore focus. A native Seal Lab dialog retains priority.
TypingEditable text uses at least 16px mobile type. Composition guards preserve IME candidate keys. Drafts stay in their existing DOM nodes through viewport transitions.
FormsHeaders and primary actions stay outside the scrolling fields, preventing a sticky action bar from covering form controls. Empty Projects have a dismissible form and a persistent New mission action.
Source handoffThe desktop header opens the source package and guide. On mobile, the same link sits in the Projects drawer, leaving the primary mission controls clear. The handoff provides a direct return to Compass.

The camera actions are folded behind View and use two rows on compact screens. The workspace dock yields to modal sheets and the keyboard; it restores the original controls to their desktop placement when leaving the mobile layout. Safe-area insets, visual viewport width/height, and viewport offsets position sheets around available screen space. The visual viewport keyboard heuristic is used for layout behavior; it is not a claim that every iOS keyboard has been reproduced in testing.

Replay and adaptive views — incoming implementation

  • A mission could render between its opening event and its first council seat. An empty seal signature incorrectly looked initialized, so rendering accessed missing SVG nodes and interrupted replay. Both the focused-project and overview constructors now initialize that state correctly.

  • Changing the focused project reset playback to the live edge. Focus-only entry now preserves the shared cursor and playing/paused state; explicit trace import/reset remains a separate transition.

  • Event-driven refreshes reset the previous frame timestamp. One frame owner now preserves elapsed replay time across events while camera smoothing uses its own bounded animation delta.

  • Inactive projects could show later state than the replay cursor. Scrubbing, playback, jumps, live transitions, and retracing now seek the visible Projects consistently. Delayed reports are retained in the trace without advancing a replay that has not reached them.

  • The mobile canvas relied on fixed height deductions and permanently exposed camera controls. The adaptive dock reuses the existing controls, folds camera actions on demand, and derives canvas height from available space. Compact, short-landscape, and tablet modes follow viewport shape rather than device names.

  • The selected mission's floating notes could cover its summary actions. Mobile card mode now uses one compact summary; detailed council/task/request information stays in the existing detail sheets and Activity. Camera controls temporarily replace the summary without clearing selection.

  • A scope-only toolbar resize changed the canvas after the camera had fitted it. Measured stage-height changes notify the camera about available space. In the combined contract, those notifications refit only in auto-fit mode and retain a manually adjusted camera. Focus fallback selects a visible mobile Missions action instead of the hidden desktop header action.

Historical incoming browser evidence — before the combined layout

The incoming pre-combination audit record (tests/evidence/replay-mobile-layout-audits.json) contains 57 successful settled Chrome audits, with diagnostic failures and their later fixes retained separately. There are 56 mobile/tablet audits across the 17 mobile viewport sizes listed in the matrix below, plus one 1280×800 desktop reference. The coverage includes overview, focused project, playing replay, expanded camera controls, mission browser, mission details, compact summary, and conversation drafts. It does not claim every combination of surface and size was exercised.

All recorded mobile audits found no document horizontal overflow, no fully visible enabled HTML control below 44×44 CSS pixels, and no occluded center among those controls. Every recorded primary control was fully visible and reachable. The harness excludes SVG marks and controls outside their scroll region; very short views can scroll vertically. Desktop fine-pointer targets retain desktop sizing.

Observed interactions included playback across mission opening/seating and project changes, continued playback while browsing missions, reaching the live edge, scrubbing to the start, and Go live returning to the end. Conversation draft text survived 320×568, 390×360, 852×393, and 1024×768 transitions. Camera expansion persisted through resizing. Escape restored the selected mission summary; Back to project focused the visible mobile Missions action. Scope changes refitted the overview after the measured stage height changed. The repository-only capture tests/evidence/replay-mobile-320.jpg records that workspace and is excluded from the handoff.

The record includes application source fingerprints from the incoming branch before this merge; they do not identify or validate the combined artifact. These are real historical Chrome CSS viewport checks, not physical-device, Safari, native keyboard, VoiceOver, or multitouch certification. The earlier 72-audit matrix and supplemental checks below document the preceding layout separately.

What the historical mobile review found and fixed

  • Mission browsing had no unified search/filter surface or durable mission-level navigation route.

  • Detail/familiar/agent transitions could remove the focused control or reveal new content below the visible sheet.

  • Periodic refreshes could rebuild focused agent details.

  • An empty Project's automatic New mission form could trap mobile navigation because it could not close.

  • Project editing attempted to focus an input while its sheet was still inert.

  • Crossing a desktop/mobile breakpoint could dismiss the mission drawer while preserving only its query.

  • The narrow traversal toolbar hid Fit and Lock in horizontal overflow.

  • Tablet landscape switched to small desktop targets too early.

  • Message actions depended on hover and could overlap message metadata.

  • Some form disclosures, Broadcast, removal controls, and Seal Lab controls were smaller than the mobile hit-target criterion.

  • Legacy keyboard/wheel camera paths did not synchronize navigation state and the new dock.

  • Mission search and several editable surfaces lacked complete composition-key guards.

  • The one-pointer map handler could not handle pinch/pan transitions reliably; the replacement tracks pointer identity, cancellation, bounds, and camera lock.

iPhone Duo assumptions and acceptance boundary

Apple's published specifications list an outside display of 1398×2034 physical pixels and an inside display of 1878×2670 physical pixels. The Duo-oriented stress sizes above divide these by an assumed 3× ratio. Apple’s cited specifications do not establish the Safari CSS viewport or device-pixel ratio used by this test. Treat these presets as useful shape tests, not exact device profiles.

Apple describes transitions among folded/unfolded use, portrait/landscape, and Split View. The implementation handles ordinary viewport/pointer changes and retains the same DOM nodes; actual folding and multitasking events must still be exercised on hardware.

Physical-device release acceptance

These cases remain unverified. They are the next acceptance gate for a production device claim, not failures observed in the historical browser run.

CasePass criterion
Actual Duo display geometryRecord innerWidth/innerHeight, visual viewport dimensions/offsets, DPR, orientation, and safe areas on both displays; repeat the core flows at those observed sizes.
Fold/unfold with active workMission, familiar, tab, filters, draft text, caret, and scroll context remain coherent through display transitions. No sheet remains inert or offscreen.
Split View resizingDrag through supported pane widths, including the smallest permitted width; controls stay reachable and the active sheet retains focus.
Software keyboardOpen/dismiss normal and emoji keyboards, rotate while typing, switch fields, select text, and use predictive text. Input and primary action stay visible without page jumps or input zoom.
Real IME and dictationJapanese/Chinese composition, candidate arrows, Escape, hardware Return, and dictation do not prematurely submit, dismiss, or move focus.
Multi-touchTwo-finger pinch plus translation, adding/removing fingers, pointer cancellation, interruption, and pinch at zoom limits remain stable. Single-finger page/sheet scrolling is distinct from map manipulation.
Safari navigation gesturesEdge Back/Forward and reload restore the intended route without an obscuring drawer or abandoned focus.
VoiceOverRotor order, selected tabs, live announcements, nested sheets, form labels/errors, agent reveal, and focus return are usable without sight.
Text and accessibility settingsLarger Text/page zoom, Reduce Motion, and Increase Contrast preserve reading, hit targets, and task completion at short heights.
Sustained useExercise repeated gestures, long conversation history, mission switches, and background/foreground recovery; record frame pacing, memory, thermal behavior, and battery impact. No device performance claim has been made from the current checks.

No physical iPhone, Safari/WebKit run, on-screen iOS keyboard, actual folding hardware, VoiceOver session, or native application packaging evidence is established by this handoff. Historical browser captures and source-fixture success must not substitute for that evidence.

Reproduce the checks

Run the current source suite and crown check; record their actual outcomes rather than copying the historical test total:

node scripts/check-source.mjs
node --test tests/*.test.cjs
node scripts/test-atlas-crown.mjs

When permitted browser access is available, start sites-preview from the checkout following the Sites workflow. Temporarily copy tests/mobile-qa.html to dist/__mobile-qa.html, open that exact preview page, choose a preset, perform the user interaction, and select Audit visible layout. The harness does not click or type inside the Site. Its iframe remains loaded during resizing so draft and selection retention can be checked. These are reproduction instructions for an available, authorized browser environment; they do not bypass the current policy block or imply a new browser run occurred.

Remove dist/__mobile-qa.html before packaging. Only the Site itself belongs in the deployed static directory. Keep the source harness and evidence in tests/.

Primary references

  • Apple — iPhone Duo: display/orientation transitions and Split View use cases.

  • Apple Human Interface Guidelines — Buttons: touch-target and interaction guidance. The web audit uses a 44×44 CSS-pixel criterion, while Apple's native guidance is expressed in points.

  • WebKit — New WebKit Features in Safari 13: Pointer Events and VisualViewport background. API availability is not evidence that this Site has passed physical Safari acceptance.

examples/README.md

Proposed adapter examples

These JSON files are documentation fixtures, not canonical OpenCoven schemas, endpoints, credentials, grants, or executable requests. No production API mapping was verified while preparing them. Every identifier beginning with fixture: is invented sample data. Dates are illustrative and must not be reused as live authorization windows.

  • proposed-atlas-projection.json (proposed-atlas-projection.json) separates a daemon-shaped read projection from the client’s connection/freshness observation. It demonstrates a disconnected, stale view of a mission awaiting a decision. That old observation does not prove the remote attempt is currently stopped.

  • proposed-command-intent.json (proposed-command-intent.json) shows a locally drafted resource-limit-change intent, exact identity references and concurrency preconditions. It is deliberately expired sample data. Its draft UI state and null receipt cannot be interpreted as authoritative proposal acceptance or a committed operation.

How to use them

First locate the actual canonical contract and SDK types. Create a mapping table from every relevant field here to its real owner/type, or mark the field unsupported. Replace provisional names and enums with those bindings rather than making these examples a new schema registry. Discard a field that has no supported meaning; do not manufacture it from display labels.

Parse these files as inert test data only. Neither their producer_hint nor their supplied revision strings establish trust. The application must derive authenticated transport context, scope and freshness from the canonical session/envelope behavior. Credentials and final authority decisions are outside a client intent payload. ui_hints describe a fixture’s presentation and are never enforcement.

Use them to test unavailable/stale rendering, pending-versus-committed presentation, fixture identity binding, and rejection of unrecognized operation names. They do not exercise authentication, daemon persistence, replay protection, lease enforcement or external effects. See security and authority and open decisions before introducing a live adapter.
